item.title: Amazon has a plan to index the world’s online shopping data
item.description: Amazon has plans to build a vault of data on every product sold anywhere on the internet, even products Amazon doesn't sell, and make the information available through its own site, according to Reuters . The project, called the "World Product Graph," is meant to make it less likely that shoppers leave Amazon to do their product research on Reddit or Google, and make it more likely shoppers end up at Amazon even if they're searching for a product sold elsewhere. The same goes for AI agents - if Amazon has the largest stockpile of shopping data, AI agents may rely on its index of products over others, so even people shopping with bots will end … Read the full story at The Verge.

item.title: France hold nerve to edge past South Africa in thriller
item.description: France were magnificent in attack in the first half but did not score a point in the second [Getty Images] Nations Championship France (21) 21 Tries: Grandidier-Nkanang, Attissogbe, Bielle-Biarrey Cons: Lucu (3) South Africa (7) 19 Tries: Wessels, Reinach, Marx Cons: Feinberg-Mngomezulu (2) France held on to end their five-match losing run against South Africa at Stade de France with an enthralling 21-19 victory in Paris. The victory dents the world champions' hopes of reaching the Nations Championship final and puts Les Bleus in a strong position to top the northern hemisphere standings. The hosts, inspired by their captain Antoine Dupont, showed their class and skill to score three first-half tries in an action-packed game. France's back three of Aaron Grandidier-Nkanang, Theo Attissogbe and Louis Bielle-Biarrey all crossed in a thrilling opening 40 minutes, with Jan-Hendrik Wessels scoring off the back of a maul for the visitors. The Springboks thought they had a second try on the stroke of half-time but Kurt-Lee Arendse's try was chalked off after he strayed marginally offside. Number eight Jasper Wiese was shown a 20-minute red card early in the second half - the third of four cards shown the game - for a shoulder charge, but it had the opposite effect to derailing the world champions. With South Africa's set-piece power proving too much, replacement scrum-half Cobus Reinach and hooker Malcolm Marx scored to set up a thrilling finale. However, Manie Libbok missed the vital conversion to Marx's try that would have levelled the game. With South Africa pushing for a winning score, Bielle-Biarrey produced a huge defensive tackle to force the ball loose, before Dupont, who was named player of the match, gathered possession to help seal the victory. The result will come as a blow to both England and Ireland, who are in direct competition with France for a place in the Nations Championship final at the end of the month. Les Bleus, who are six points clear at the top of the northern hemisphere standings, now face Argentina next Saturday, putting them in a strong position to reach the inaugural final at Allianz Stadium on Sunday, 29 November. Bielle-Biarrey delivered the crucial tackle to win France the game [Getty Images] Dupont wears 10 but excels from nine Injuries to France's three first-choice fly-halves - Matthieu Jalibert, Romain Ntamack and Antoine Hastoy - left France coach Fabien Galthie with little option but to deploy his captain and talismanic scrum-half at number 10. Despite wearing the France number 10 shirt for the first time, Dupont lined up at scrum-half, as Galthie played Rassie Erasmus, who had swapped his entire front row an hour before kick-off, at his own game. It was an electric start from the hosts, as a clever move sent Kalvin Gourgues through a gap, with Grandidier-Nkanang eventually crossing in the corner. A monstrous left-footed 50:22 from Dupont, with South Africa lock Lood de Jager in the sin-bin for a high tackle, gave

item.title: Nations Championship: Fixtures and standings
item.description: France ended South Africa's 100% record in the Nations Championship with a sensational 21-19 victory over the world champions at the Stade de France on Friday. Les Bleus' fourth victory from five pool matches extended their lead in the northern hemisphere standings to six points with one game to play. South Africa remain top of the standings in the southern hemisphere but will be overtaken by New Zealand if the All Blacks beat Wales in Cardiff on Saturday. England will hope to close the gap to France when they face Japan at Allianz Stadium on Saturday. Steve Borthwick's side are in second place on points difference in the northern pool after an emphatic 45-22 victory over Australia last weekend. Ireland secured a 42-12 win over Argentina and are third, with Fiji their visitors in Dublin on Saturday. Scotland, who lost to New Zealand last week, are in fourth place with two wins and two defeats and face Australia at Murrayfield on Sunday. Wales overcame Japan 28-21 in their first home match of the championship, but remain in fifth place. France will be favourites to secure their place in the inaugural final when they face Argentina in the last round of pool matches on 21 November. The finals weekend takes place from 27-29 November, with all six matches at Allianz Stadium and the title match bringing the championship to a conclusion. Feyi-Waboso burns bright as England energy endorses Borthwick Scotland's familiar frailties brutally exposed in All Blacks schooling Standings Autumn fixtures & results Friday, 6 November Ireland 42-12 Argentina Saturday, 7 November Italy 7-66 South Africa Scotland 21-43 New Zealand Wales 28-21 Japan France 54-17 Fiji Sunday, 8 November England 45-22 Australia Friday, 13 November France 21-19 South Africa Saturday, 14 November Italy v Argentina (11:40 GMT) Wales v New Zealand (14:10 GMT) England v Japan (16:40 GMT) Ireland v Fiji (20:10 GMT) Sunday, 15 November Scotland v Australia (15:10 GMT) Saturday, 21 November England v New Zealand (14:10 GMT) Scotland v Japan (14:10 GMT) Ireland v South Africa (16:40 GMT) Italy v Fiji (16:40 GMT) France v Argentina (20:10 GMT) Wales v Australia (20:10 GMT) Why Wales have a lot to prove despite beating Japan Ireland going from strength to strength - Murray What is the Nations Championship? The Nations Championship pits the northern hemisphere teams who compete in the Six Nations - England, Ireland, Scotland, Wales, France and Italy - against southern hemisphere giants South Africa, New Zealand, Australia and Argentina, plus invited sides Fiji and Japan. All teams will play each of the six in the opposing hemisphere once, with three rounds of fixtures staged in July and another three in November. Their results will rank the teams within their own hemisphere, from one to six. On the final weekend in November, there is a three-day play-off event staged at Allianz Stadium in Twickenham. item.title: Rhamondre Stevenson Could Beat The Odds For Munich Game
item.description: David Butler II-Imagn Images Rhamondre Stevenson is not staying on the sideline for long. The Patriots running back worked off to the side during a walkthrough in Germany on Thursday. This move signals a return much sooner than the initial knee injury reports suggested. Pats Pulpit noted his presence offers real optimism for Sunday’s matchup against the Detroit Lions. He is expected to miss a couple of weeks after the injury in Week 9. He suffered the issue late in the third quarter of the 45-27 loss to the Green Bay Packers. Reports say the knee tendon problem near the back of his knee did not need surgery. Yet the media got the timeline wrong, according to Drake Maye. “I think that just speaks to, first off, the media not really knowing 100% what they’re talking about a lot of the time,” Maye said. Teammates See The Grind The locker room knows Stevenson wants to be back on the field. He is trying to help the team win a big one before the bye week arrives. Maye described him as a great player who can help the squad right now. “This is a time for players, a lot of the players on this team that are trying to get out there, play with their teammates and knowing that he’s a great player and can help us out,” Maye added. Teammate DeMario Douglas sees the work ethic up close. He called Stevenson a dawg who refuses to quit. “I know some people that probably be like, ‘Man, I ain’t even going to try’, you but his situation, man, I be talking to him [and he’s] like, ‘I’m going to try. I’m going to do what I can do.’ He’s working, he’s getting better. So, when the time comes, I know he’s working to get better,” Douglas said. Reality Check For Fantasy Owners Optimism is high, but the medical reality remains tricky. According to RotoBaller, it would be quite shocking if Stevenson plays during Week 10. Fantasy managers must continue to anticipate that Stevenson will remain inactive this weekend. Should he fail to receive approval to play in Germany, Corey Kiner will replace him as New England’s primary back facing the Lions. The Patriots face the Lions on Sunday, Nov. 15, at 9:30 a.m. ET in Munich.

item.title: Dupont praises France late grind in South Africa victory
item.description: France captain Antoine Dupont was all over the pitch, according to his coach Fabien Galthie (Anne-Christine POUJOULAT) France captain Antoine Dupont said on Friday that beating Rugby World Cup holders South Africa 21-19 was important to show that his side are capable of grinding out victories when it matters. Dupont's outfit held off a stirring second-half Springbok comeback in Paris to remain top of the northern hemisphere table in the Nations Championship having come into the fixture as underdogs. The half-back, who turns 31 on Sunday, put in a player of the match performance as Les Bleus kept out the visitors with a last-gasp defensive effort, succeeding where they had failed in a World Cup quarter-final lost by a single point three years ago. "In the head it's important to win matches that count, that are tough, that go down to the last minute," Dupont told broadcaster TF1. "It shows the mentality of the team that never gave in, even if we had it hard on our line," the 2021 World Rugby player of the year added. Dupont was named to start the game at fly-half for a first time in international rugby with France down to their fifth-choice playmaker after Romain Ntamack's injury in last weekend's win over Fiji. Despite wearing the number 10 jersey, Toulouse's Dupont featured in his regular scrum-half position with Maxime Lucu in the nine shirt but deputising for Ntamack. Head coach Fabien Galthie paid tribute to his captain, joking that he had been all over the pitch playing in several positions. He even helped hold up South African flanker Pieter-Steph du Toit over the line to deny South Africa a try and won a crucial turnover to see out the game. "Sometimes I call him a good back rower, he doesn't like that much but he was a good back rower today," said Galthie. "He played at nine, a little bit of 10, and a good six. "And he kicked well. A six who can kick as well -- the complete package. "He doesn't want to play at hooker, but if you ask me, he played a bit in every position. "He nailed his match, he wanted to do that." - 'We killed our dreams' - South Africa coach Rassie Erasmus could not hide his disappointment at losing their perfect record in the tournament, having picked up the maximum five points in their previous four matches. "If we scored one more try, we would have got five points from this game and we would have been in the running" to top the northern hemisphere group and reach the final at Twickenham in two weeks' time, Erasmus said. "We basically killed our dreams for the Nations Cup tonight with this performance and not getting the win and the fourth try. "Maybe they were also in that mindset of getting four tries and trying to top the Northern League." Erasmus said his team had not lacked much to come away with a victory. "Them playing very well and we didn't play well, so I can't find a lot of excuses," he said. "They were on top of their game and we were a little bit off... one point here, one point there. item.title: Billy Horschel And Chris Kirk Face The Harsh Reality Of The FedEx Cup Cutoff
item.description: Jim Dedmon-Imagn Images The clock has run out on excuses for the players hovering near the bottom of the FedEx Cup standings. Just two tournaments remain for golfers to earn playing privileges for the 2027 season, and the margin for error is gone. The autumn swing is not a holiday; it is used to identify golfers who are not ready for the main stage. The Bubble Boys Are Real Max Greyserman sits at No. 97, holding his status by a thread after a rough 2026 campaign. He managed a T10 and a T11 finish in the fall to stay inside the magic number, but that is not enough to feel safe. Billy Horschel, an eight-time winner, has not recorded an individual top-10 finish this year. He sat out the summer of 2025 with an injury and has struggled to regain his old form. Horschel has four top-15 finishes since the Canadian Open, yet he missed the cut in Cabo. These next two venues should suit his style better, but the pressure is immense. Chris Kirk faces a different challenge as the No. 102 ranked player. Should any golfer shift from outside to inside across the next two competitions, Kirk stands as the top prospect. The consequences are evident: conditional status or a drop to lower tours awaits them unless they rediscover the game that secured their PGA Tour spot. Success Is Not Guaranteed Some players have already locked up their status for years to come. Austin Smotherman won two tournaments this fall and secured his spot through the 2029 season. Jacob Bridgeman and Michael Brennan also added to their season tallies, proving they belong. But the spotlight belongs to the losers right now, not the winners. For fortunate golfers holding status from past achievements yet lacking guarantees, autumn brings the suffering of the previous year. The Austin Championship and the RSM Classic will decide the fate of these players in the coming weeks. The 2027 season is just around the corner, and there is no time for a slow start. The top 125 in the FedEx Cup gets conditional status, which is a scary place to be for anyone who wants to make a living on tour. The field is deep, and the competition is fierce as the PGA Tour wraps up its season. Only the best will survive the final cut line. Only two events remain for competitors to secure playing rights for the 2027 campaign.

item.title: Texas football team unable to leave Austin for LSU game because of FAA shutdown
item.description: An American Airlines pilot flies the Texas Longhorns flag as the team arrives at Louis Armstrong International Airport on Wednesday, Dec. 27, 2023 in New Orleans, Louisiana. The Texas Longhorns will face the Washington Huskies in the Sugar Bowl on January 1, 2024. (Aaron E. Martinez/American-Statesman) On Friday afternoon, the Texas football team remained stuck in Austin ahead of its planned trip to LSU . On Friday, the Federal Aviation Administration halted all air travel because of a communication issue. That decision impacted the Longhorns, who had boarded their American Airlines plane ahead of Saturday night's game at LSU. COLUMN : Why I'm taking Arch Manning to make the difference Saturday A team spokesperson confirmed to the American-Statesman that the team's plane was indeed grounded and the Longhorns were still awaiting word on when they can leave. Citing sources, Horns247 also reported that Texas players, coaches and staffers had deplaned and headed back to the team facilities. Texas is set to play LSU at 6:30 p.m. Saturday. This is a developing story that will be updated. Sign up for the Daily Briefing from the Austin American-Statesman. Start your day with the must-read headlines from Austin's most trusted news source. This article originally published at Texas football team unable to leave Austin for LSU game because of FAA shutdown .

item.title: FAA ground stop does not affect Wisconsin football game vs Maryland
item.description: Wisconsin football has made it safely to Maryland as the FAA’s nationwide ground stop affects travel for many other Week 11 college football games. The Badgers ’ team charter flight took off from Madison’s Dane County Regional Airport at 1:58 p.m. CT and landed in Baltimore at 4:43 p.m. ET, per UW sports information. The FAA issued the ground stop on the afternoon of Nov. 13, citing an air traffic control issue that led to extraordinary circumstances and safety concerns . U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said in a tweet that it is a communication issue that impacts all air traffic control centers. Other Big Ten road teams were not as fortunate as the Badgers . Minnesota, Purdue and Washington have been affected, according to ESPN’s Pete Thamel , ahead of their respective games against Penn State, Iowa and Michigan State. A Big Ten spokesman told Thamel that all of the league’s officials are on site and not affected by the FAA ground stop. This article originally appeared on Milwaukee Journal Sentinel: FAA ground stop does not affect Wisconsin football game vs Maryland

item.title: Lynch: Remembering Dan Hicks | Opinion
item.description: A few years back, I sat next to Dan Hicks in an Orlando steakhouse talking about working in television, which he’d been doing to acclaim for decades and I, stutteringly, for a hot minute. I asked a question that I often put to accomplished companions at dinner: what was the worst screw-up from which he learned the most? He didn’t hesitate to search for an answer. Dan recalled one of his earliest assignments in golf for NBC Sports, at what was then known as the Bob Hope Chrysler Classic. He was emceeing the trophy presentation on the 18th green, during which he was to be alongside the tournament host, who even then was well stricken in years. Ahead of the ceremony, he received a final word of advice from Tommy Roy, the longtime NBC golf producer. “Do not, under any circumstances,” Roy told him, “lose the microphone.” Sitting in that restaurant years later, Hicks gave a comical account of a tug-of-war that went entirely unnoticed by viewers. As he welcomed in Hope, Dan hovered his stick mic closer to the legendary entertainer so that he might offer a few words. Hope attempted to take it. Dan held on. Almost imperceptibly, Hope tugged a little harder. Smile fixed, Dan kept a Vulcan death grip. In the end, he lost out to guile and experience when Hope snatched the mic and turned to address the crowd. Dan described hearing an anguished, guttural groan in his earpiece from the production truck. “Uggghhhhh.” What remained of the broadcast would now run on Bob Hope’s schedule, not Tommy Roy’s. That was the last time Dan lost control of the microphone, which he wielded with assurance and diligence until his unexpected passing on Nov. 11 at the age of 64. His was a career that seemed to have precious few screw-ups that might be rendered fodder for laughs over dinner, but he’d probably argue the over on that. A summer evening in St Andrews with Dan, 2022. We joked about being the only guys in the photo without a PGA Tour win. pic.twitter.com/919WqGzmzt — Eamon Lynch (@eamonlynch) November 12, 2026 For more than three decades, he was the soundtrack to some indelible memories for sports fans, whether they were following the exploits of Tiger Woods, Michael Phelps, or Notre Dame football. He knew exactly what to say and — just as importantly — when to say nothing at all. Some of his finest moments have been played on a loop in recent days, like the “Expect anything different?” call as Woods forced a playoff at the 2008 U.S. Open, and the frantic closing seconds of the men’s swimming relay race at the Olympics that same summer. The blessing of having excelled in a high-profile job is that he leaves an admirable body of work through which he will be remembered. Others have memories that are more personal, but equally enduring. My relationship with Dan was one of casual friendship. He’d text occasionally about a column he’d read or show he’d seen, or to joke about Brad Faxon’s fashion sense (sorry, Brad!). I’d study him to see what I could learn, admitting to him

item.title: Queta’s Rise And Historic Road Trip Prove Celtics Depth Is Real
item.description: Dan Hamilton-Imagn Images The Boston Celtics just did something no one in franchise history has ever done. They swept a four-game road trip with a plus-86 point differential, the best mark the team has ever posted in such a span. This wasn’t just a lucky streak; it was a masterclass in resilience. The team erased a 22-point deficit to beat the Toronto Raptors 98-93 on Wednesday night, improving their record to 10-2 overall, according to New Hampshire Union Leader . Most teams would crumble after such a big hole. The Celtics did the opposite. They rallied to win their fifth straight game, showing a poise that goes beyond simple talent. Joe Mazzulla credited the whole group for the win. He noted that even the bench players who did not see court time provided a massive lift in energy. The Big Man Steps Up With Paul George out due to illness, the big man stepped into the starting role alongside Luka Garza. Queta finished with 11 points, 13 rebounds, and three blocks against the Raptors. He also showed an expanded shooting touch, hitting three 3-pointers this season, which is already a career high for him. Derrick White praised Queta’s growth and impact on both ends of the floor. Queta agreed that the team feeds off each other’s energy. He noted that many players made energy plays that galvanize teammates and that feeding off each other is something the team needs to do more to get over the hump most nights. Depth That Wins Games This win was a full-team effort, not just a star-driven display. Mitchell Robinson was seen cheering on his teammates during the postgame scrum, offering high praise to White and Queta after the big man sealed the game with two free throws. The locker room vibe stayed high even after a flight delay, with players like Payton Pritchard and Ron Harper Jr. running the DJ duties for the postgame jam session. The Celtics have now won 9 of their last 10 games, a stretch that includes a 7-1 run over eight games in 13 days. This depth and ability to win tight games show why they are playing 11 guys every night and leaning on such a deep roster to chase a title.

item.title: Philip Rivers’ introductory press conference set for Monday
item.description: RALEIGH, NORTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 29: Former NC State quarterback Philip Rivers attends the game between the North Carolina Tar Heels and the NC State Wolfpack at Carter-Finley Stadium on November 29, 2025 in Raleigh, North Carolina. (Photo by Lance King/Getty Images) | Getty Images NC State made it official today that Philip Rivers will be the football program’s next head coach, and he will be introduced on Monday afternoon at 1:30 p.m. ET. ACC Network will carry the press conference live. Rivers’ deal with NC State is reportedly worth $3.25 million annually over five seasons, and the buyout is his salary multiplied by the number of years remaining on his deal. This part of the risk, at least, is relatively inexpensive. From NC State’s press release : “I am humbled and honored to be the next head football coach at NC State University,” Rivers said. “In many ways, I feel like I’m coming home. This is where it all began for me as an 18-year-old kid from Alabama, and now to return to this great place as head coach is beyond words. “I gave it everything I had here as a player for 51 games and I will give it everything I have as the coach. There’s no denying that this is going to take hard work, but we’re not scared of hard. I look forward to getting after it every single day with an unbelievable coaching staff and a group of players who are dedicated to relentlessly pursuing victory.” Philip is one of the most competitive guys out there, and hopefully he can channel that in the right way in this new position, because it’s going to be a lot for him. As with all new coaching hires, I’ll be cautiously optimistic until proven otherwise.

item.title: Dodgers Legend Orel Hershiser Reveals Why LA Will Fight to Keep Tarik Skubal
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers legend Orel Hershiser talked to Dodgers Nation in an exclusive interview about his outlook on Tarik Skubal’s free agency. As a key member of the Sportsnet LA broadcast and someone who has been around the team for decades, Hershiser knows what it takes to deliver when pitching at The Ravine. In his eyes, Skubal is the kind of guy who has more to show Dodgers fans , beyond his 2.61 ERA in his 10 appearances. Why he thinks the Dodgers will be aggressive to keep Skubal While Skubal was certainly good overall and great in stretches, he wasn’t the pitcher who won two straight Cy Young awards. Sep 17, 2026; Cincinnati, Ohio, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Tarik Skubal celebrates after clinching the National League West title after the game against the Cincinnati Reds at Great American Ball Park. Mandatory Credit: Aaron Doster-Imagn Images That guy, Hershiser says, is still there, and it will show whenever he pitches next. “I don’t think we’ve seen his best yet, and I think they will try as hard as they can to sign him because what we saw was a guy who fit into a team with amazing chemistry, and he fit right in,” Hershiser told Dodgers Nation. Beyond his fit, Hershiser, nicknamed the “Bulldog,” sees grit in Skubal that earned the Hall of Famer’s respect. “What we saw was a guy who couldn’t wait to take the ball. Even though he’s going to be a free agent, he would have come back on short rest,” Hershiser said. “He would have pitched multiple times. He would have pitched deeper into games than you normally would want him to, if you were thinking about the long term and his health.” View this post on Instagram A post shared by Dodgers Nation (@dodgersnation) While not going as far as to predict Skubal would return, Herischier was not shy about noting that he is a player the Dodgers typically pursue aggressively. “I think we saw a very, very competitive guy, a very, very professional guy, a great student of the game, and a great teammate. And I think all of that increases his value, and the Dodgers would want him.” Oct 20, 1988; Oakland, CA, USA: FILE PHOTO; Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Orel Hershiser reacts after defeating the Oakland Athletics in the 1988 World Series at Oakland-Alameda County Coliseum. Hershiser was named series MVP. Mandatory Credit: MPS-USA TODAY Sports The Skubal-Hershiser parallels Hershiser knows a thing or two about what it takes to be at the top of a rotation and carry the mantle of being a Cy Young Award winner. He and Skubal share that honor, along with the ability to claim they were the best pitcher alive for years. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Dodgers Nation (@dodgersnation) Hershiser was part of the Dodgers’ last golden era, during which the franchise won its last title since the 2020s. Looking ahead to 2027 and beyond, if he stays, Skubal could cement himself as the next feisty Dodgers ace to bring a title to Los Angeles — as Koufax, Kershaw, and even Hershiser did.

item.title: Senne Lammens opens up on Michael Carrick’s sack
item.description: Senne Lammens opens up on Michael Carrick’s sack Michael Carrick paid the ultimate price for Manchester United’s dismal start to the season, with the Red Devils languishing in 18th position in the Premier League after winning only once so far. The former head coach received his marching orders amid complaints about the squad’s poor fitness levels and tactical blunders. INEOS’ role in this whole fiasco cannot be taken lightly, as they failed to back the Englishman in the summer. Add to this key players underperforming, and such a scenario was bound to happen. One of last season’s top performers , goalkeeper Senne Lammens, has struggled to replicate that form , with the Belgian failing to keep a single clean sheet in the league. Lammens on INEOS’ call to sack Carrick He arguably had the worst game of his United career so far against Aston Villa, in what turned out to be Carrick’s final game in charge. The 24-year-old was asked about Carrick’s dismissal after his country’s international friendly against Türkiye. He explained that INEOS’ decision was a tough pill to swallow for the whole squad, which had shown through recent results that they were fully behind the former United midfielder. “Yes, these are difficult weeks. I’m not going to lie about that,” he admitted. “Of course, as a Manchester United team, we need to do better. Why United were forced to sack Carrick “Now the manager has been sacked. It’s obviously a difficult time, both for me and for the whole team. We were all behind him.” After the Bournemouth debacle, United’s co-owners had reportedly handed Carrick a three-game ultimatum . It started in disastrous fashion. The 20-time English league champions showed promise in the first half against Chelsea before Lisandro Martínez single-handedly dragged his team down. A trademark comeback in the Champions League against AS Roma followed, and despite a come-from-behind 4-4 draw against Aston Villa, INEOS decided to pull the plug. Mauricio Pochettino has a mountain to climb, with INEOS reportedly expecting European football at the end of the season despite the fact that the Argentine is inheriting a weak and broken squad . online polls

item.title: Joshua Kimmich insists he has “no problems” with his ankle after dangerous tackle
item.description: Photo by Christian Charisius/picture alliance via Getty Images Joshua Kimmich received a heavy tackle from substitute Vanja Dragojević in the 76th minute of Germany’s 3-1 UEFA Nations League victory against Serbia. Kimmich went down clutching his ankle leaving German — and especially Bayern — fans holding their breath. The German captain managed to finish the game. However, many remained concerned there could have been some damage to the midfielder’s joint. In a post-match interview, Kimmich eased worries. When asked whether the knock he took would be an issue ahead of Germany’s high-stakes clash against the Netherlands on Monday, Kimmich insisted he had “no problems” with his ankle. “No, there are no problems at all,” said the 31-year-old midfielder (via @iMiaSanMia ). Bayern Munich already have a laundry list of injuries. The last thing Die Rekordmeister needed was an injury to their midfield lynchpin. Thankfully, it appears Kimmich is healthy. However, It does remind one of how costly these international breaks can be. One bad challenge is all it takes to end a player’s season. Join the conversation! item.title: Cowboys’ 4-5 Record Shows Disappointing Halfway Point
item.description: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images The Dallas Cowboys reached the halfway mark of the 2026 season with a record that leaves fans asking hard questions. A recent win over the Indianapolis Colts kept playoff hopes alive, but the team sits at 4-5 overall. This standing places them in a precarious spot within the conference race. The victory did lift the team up three spots in the NFC standings, per Blogging The Boys . Yet, the loss to Arizona and Tampa Bay earlier this year still weighs heavily on their resume. Those two defeats make it vital that the Cowboys stay ahead of those rivals moving forward. The Standings Reality Check Dallas currently holds the tenth spot in the big picture of the 2026 NFC Playoff Standings according to Blogging The Boys. A drop to 4-6 is likely if they lose to the conference-leading 49ers this week. Such a slide could allow teams with 3-6 records to creep back above Dallas in the rankings. It is only Week 10, so there is still ample time to rectify the situation, per the same report. However, the margin for error has vanished for a team with big-market expectations. High Stakes Against San Francisco The upcoming matchup features the conference-leading 49ers visiting AT&T Stadium on Sunday. This game is a critical test for a squad that has struggled to maintain consistency. The pressure is on to prove that the recent win over Indy was more than a fluke. Fans need to see a team that can handle a top-tier opponent without falling apart. The Cowboys must win this game to keep their name in the hunt for a wild card spot. According to Blogging The Boys, unless a massive upset occurs, a likely fall to 4-6 might let certain 3-6 squads surpass them in the rankings. The Cowboys host the conference-leading 49ers this week, which sets the stage for a must-win scenario. A loss here would deepen the crisis for a roster that promised more before the season started. The clock is ticking on the 2026 campaign, and the next game defines the rest of it. The Cowboys are currently 4-5 (2-4) in the 2026 NFC standings, per Blogging The Boys.

item.title: Cowboys aggressiveness on offense must be turned up vs. 49ers
item.description: Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images | Getty Images After two straight weeks of early window kickoffs in which the Dallas Cowboys had to fight, claw, scratch, and get knocked down to go 1-1 against the Arizona Cardinals and Indianapolis Colts, they play in the Sunday late afternoon window against the San Francisco 49ers. Both teams are off a win, which puts the Cowboys right back in a position they’ve been time and time again and failed in nearly every time, trying to win consecutive games under Brian Schottenheimer. The Cowboys can’t afford to spin their wheels much longer if they want to make this season mean something though. This 49ers matchup is exactly that opportunity for the Cowboys, so let’s get to how they can pull off the upset. The Dallas Cowboys will beat the San Francisco 49ers if… …they win on 1st down on both offense and defense. Think for a second about how many NFL offenses are truly earning the label of “elite”, “scary”, or “explosive” right now, then without looking at any other metrics or analytics consider the top four tiers in the first downs per play category. They are the Bills, 49ers, Lions, and Bengals tied for first, the Cowboys in second, and the Jaguars and Rams in third just ahead of the Patriots and Chiefs. Also among these teams, the 49ers, Lions, and Bills are in the top five for fewest third downs faced per game. The Patriots, Chiefs, Jags, and Bengals are all virtually tied with the Bills to round out the top nine. Then there are the 14th ranked Cowboys, much closer to teams like the Steelers, Texans, and Browns – none of which have the QB situation Dallas does that should be keeping them out of this not-so-great company. This is a main culprit why they feel like outliers on the elite, scary, or explosive list while the other offenses are much more deserving. For even more evidence that the Cowboys offense is all about Dak right now, and that Prescott should be getting way more help than he is from all directions, there’s the fact two of the three touchdown drives last week at the Colts came in two minute situations before halftime and at the end of the game. The Cowboys need much more than just Prescott to be at their absolute best against the 49ers, but fairly or not will also need #4 to be among the players that elevates their game this week as well. The best path towards doing so is much more early down aggressiveness and the Cowboys embracing what they do best by throwing the ball to CeeDee Lamb, and hopefully George Pickens, not just on third down, but all the time. Without Jake Ferguson for this game, one of the things the Cowboys are going to have an incredibly difficult time doing is persuading the 49ers defense out of loading the box. They don’t have the middle of the field threat to get behind these stacked looks, especially considering the freakish coverage ability to all parts of the field from Fred Warner. Dallas will still need to find it’s times to run the ball and doing so well on early downs wou

item.title: Brajan Gruda on his dream debut goal for Germany
item.description: BELGRADE, SERBIA - NOVEMBER 13: Brajan Gruda of Germany celebrates scoring his team’s third goal during the UEFA Nations League 2026/27 group phase match between Serbia and Germany at Rajko Mitic Stadium on November 13, 2026 in Belgrade, Serbia. (Photo by Maja Hitij/Getty Images) | Getty Images Brajan Gruda is in dreamland. The 22-year-old German forward had his breakout a few seasons ago for Mainz — earning rave reviews from Bayern Munich and national team legend Thomas Müller at the time — but his career has taken a circuitous path since. His big move to England did not pay off, at least not quickly, and after a nondescript season-and-a-half at Brighton, Gruda found himself back in the Bundesliga, this time on loan at RB Leipzig. But this year, it is all starting to come together. New Germany boss Jürgen Klopp has been keen on incorporating the dynamic attacker’s skills into the men’s national team setup; Gruda narrowly missed a call-up in September due to injury to Klopp’s super-sized squad. But his season at Leipzig has been promising — two goals and five assists across all competitions. When Klopp trimmed the roster for his second international period, Gruda still made the cut. Now he is taking his break and running with it. Friday against Serbia in a quiet, rain-sodden Belgrade stadium (largely devoid of fans owing to a UEFA spectator ban for the match), Gruda earned a place in Klopp’s XI for his Germany debut. He left having terrorized the Serbian defenses with a man-of-the-match performance, and collecting a dazzling goal after dribbling halfway down the pitch. All while being the man to don the #10 shirt — which he is fitting very, very well in. “Jo [Kimmich] was on the ball, and with my first touch, I moved inside,” Gruda said of his higlight-reel moment (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ). “There was so much space that I thought I had to take advantage of it. And the fact that they weren’t closing me down was good for me too, so I simply made the most of it. It was instinct. I don’t think too much when I’m dribbling. I just do it. I don’t think there’s really time to think anyway. It just happens. That’s it.” Gruda’s effort put Germany up 3-0 after just 50 minutes, proving to be the dagger en route to a commanding 3-1 win . The way he’s playing, there is sure to be much more to come. Join the conversation! Sign up for a user account and get: New, improved notifications system! item.title: Kenneth Walker Injury Threatens Chiefs’ Rushing Momentum
item.description: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images Kenneth Walker III, the running back for the Kansas City Chiefs, missed Friday practice because of a sore groin, casting doubt on his availability for Sunday’s game. The team lacks a top rusher after an injury created a gap in the lineup. In his first season with the squad, Walker has accumulated 872 rushing yards, trailing the league lead by just eight yards. His per-game average of 109 yards leads the entire NFL, so his absence would be a major blow if he cannot play. Reid Backs the Rookie Head coach Andy Reid knows the pressure is on, yet he remains calm about the backup plan. Reid stated that the team will monitor Walker’s condition leading into Sunday, but he is not panicking about the loss of production. “He’s going to play anyway, whether Ken’s there or not,” Reid said regarding the game plan. The coach has total faith in the young players ready to step up if the starter cannot go. “Everybody has confidence in him,” Reid added when asked about the depth chart. Rookie Emmett Johnson is the name on everyone’s lips if Walker sits out. Johnson is a fifth-round pick out of Nebraska who has already shown he can handle big touches. He has rushed for 111 yards and a touchdown on just 26 carries this season. The rookie also secured 14 catches for 237 yards and another score, demonstrating he is a complete back. Should Walker be unable to play this weekend, Johnson stands ready to assume a larger workload. Other Keys to the Game The offense has other pieces moving into place for the trip to Atlanta. Wide receiver Josh Downs plans to participate days after being traded from Indianapolis. Just before the NFL trade deadline on Tuesday, the Chiefs acquired Downs from the Colts. Reid praised the new receiver’s quick learning curve, noting, “I thought he did a nice job for what we asked him to do, to digest everything in a couple days.” Health concerns linger elsewhere, but the team expects wide receiver Xavier Worthy to be available after he left the previous game with a hamstring injury. The New Haven Register reports that the squad still lacks wide receiver Tyquan Thornton, who sits on injured reserve because of a dislocated ankle. Reid called Downs a smart kid who knows how to play. The Chiefs face the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday, Nov. 15, at 1 p.m. ET in Mercedes-Benz Stadium. According to the Associated Press, Walker has participated in one fewer game this year than the Atlanta Falcons running back, producing a distinctive statistic for the matchup. Walker has caught 22 balls for 172 yards and four touchdowns, showing his value as a receiver out of the backfield. The team will see how Walker’s sore groin holds up before making a final call on his status. “We’ll see. He’s not one to say something like that (without meaning it),” Reid said.

item.title: PREGAMIN’ GEORGIA
item.description: WELCOME BACK TO PREGAMIN’, HERE’S YOUR JAM OF THE WEEK WHEN IN JAWJA! Rock M-ixology We’re approaching Thanksgiving season, so let me make a confession… I think November is a pretty crumby time to make cocktails. The heaviness and variety of Thanksgiving staples make pairing a cocktail – already kind of a quack food science – difficult, especially when a good wine or a solid saison will do the trick. Need my real Missouri recommendation: get yourself a fresh pack of Tank 7 for Thanksgiving and thank me later. But I’ve got a Friendsgiving party coming up, and I’m responsible for the mixed drinks. So we have to steer this ship somewhere. Let’s make it friendly for all audiences and put together a simple Apple Cider Sangria. 2 cups apple cider, 1 cup apple brandy, 750 mL bottle dry white wine, chilled, 1 lemon, 3 apples, thinly sliced, 12 oz. ginger ale Nothing fancy, but it does the trick. One of the nice things about Sangria is that you can adjust your taste preferences based on how much you like the bubbly element. I probably want a tad more ginger beer than this recipe calls for, so I just top it off. A few glasses of this, and you won’t remember the Georgia game ever happened! Very recent fun fact that will win you trivia points in 50 years: Georgia governor-elect Keisha Lance Bottoms will become the United States first Black female governor when she is sworn in this coming year. Is Georgia the only program in the NCAA to have beaten a team so badly that the opposing program folded altogether? I don’t know, but they can certainly claim to have done it! Mercery University disbanded its football team in 1892 after losing its first ever football game, 50-0, to the Bulldogs. Georgia – from what I can tell, at least – is one of three schools to use the tune of “Battle Hymn of the Republic” as an official school fight song. The other two? The University of Colorado and Auburn. It should be said, however, that Georgia is the only school – again, from what I can tell – to use the tune in its primary fight song. Mizzou vibes are bad and everyone is moving on from us, so it’s clearly time for Eli Drinkwitz to say something controversial. What did you think about his, “no conferences without championship games,” take? Josh Matejka, Deputy Site Manager: I understand why people may not vibe with it. Someone on Rock M+ the other day pointed out that the Big 8 used to not have a conference championship game and everyone was fine with it. For me, though, the conference championship is an integral part of the sport. I pay attention during championship week, even when Mizzou isn’t playing (which is nearly always, unfortunately.) It’s an opportunity for season-long narrative arcs to come to a close and to see some of the best teams in the country – sometimes blue bloods, sometimes upstarts – clash. item.title: Joshua Kimmich says Germany-Netherlands match now a “final”
item.description: 13 November 2026, Serbia, Belgrad: Soccer, Men, Nations League A, Group Stage, Group 2, Matchday 5, Serbia vs. Germany, Rajko Miti Stadium, Brajan Gruda (Germany) celebrates his goalmaking the score 03with Joshua Kimmich (Germany). Photo: Christian Charisius/dpa - IMPORTANT NOTICE: In accordance with the regulations of the Bundesliga and the DFB (German Football Association), it is prohibited to use or allow the use of photographs taken in the stadium and/or during the game in the form of sequential images and/or video-like photo sequences. (Photo by Christian Charisius/picture alliance via Getty Images) In front of a largely empty Rajko Mitic Stadium in Belgrade, Germany came away with a 3-1 win over Serbia in their first of two UEFA Nations League matches during this month’s international break. An own goal from Srđan Babić in the third minute well before his consolation goal in the 56th minute opened the scoring for Germany in what was a dominant first half display aside from a spirited end from the Serbians to the first 45 minutes. Florian Wirtz added a second for Die Mannschaft in the 14th minute after tapping in from point blank range after what looked like keeper Vanja Milinković-Savić getting a hand to initial chip attempt. Brajan Gruda rounded out the scoring for Germany in the 50th minute with a moment of individual brilliance having made a 40-yard run with the ball at his feet and Jürgen Klopp had quite the smile on his face when cameras panned to the German dugout after the goal. Gruda’s goal wrapped a bow on what was Klopp’s second win since becoming Germany manager and a win that keeps the Germans in third place in Nations League group B ahead of the clash against the Netherlands in Berlin on Monday night. The Dutch will be heading to Berlin on the heels of a comprehensive 7-0 win over Greece in Amsterdam as Xavi Hernández really seems to have found his way with the Dutch national team. After the win over Serbia, Joshua Kimmich was asked whether or not he’ll be going into the match against the Netherlands with the mentality of a cup final as Germany fight to get into the second spot in the group. “Yes, absolutely. I think we actually have to win, given the current situation in the group. So we’re really looking forward to the game,” he said (via @iMiaSanMia ). A win alone over the Dutch wouldn’t guarantee second spot in the group for Germany, as they would also need Greece to not defeat Serbia in Volos. Germany do currently have a superior goal difference; the two nations are level on eight points apiece. Join the conversation! Sign up for a user account and get: New, improved notifications system! item.title: Svitolina knocks out Sabalenka to grab final spot in WTA Finals semis
item.description: The final semifinal spot in the WTA Finals was on the line Friday afternoon as Aryna Sabalenka and Elina Svitolina matched wits in a winner-take-all clash at the Indian Wells Tennis Garden. The winner's prize? A spot in Saturday's semifinals to play Linda Noskova. The loser would see her tournament come to an end. On this day it was the Ukrainian Svitolina showing unlimited resolve as she dispatched Sabalenka, the highest-ranked player in the field, with a gutsy 6-3, 3-6, 6-1 victory. After the final point and shaking the chair umpire's hand, Svitolina raised her arms in joy and stared skyward with the biggest smile she's worn in months. It's been a tumultuous time for Svitolina going through a public divorce on top of the ongoing war in her home country. But for this moment, after a thrilling win on the Stadium 2 court at Indian Wells, she could only smile. War and peace: Ukrainian Elina Svitolina finds inspiration at WTA Finals Svitolina, the No. 6 seed who won this tournament in 2018, will move into the semifinals with Mirra Andreeva (3), Jessica Pegula (5) and Linda Noskova (8). The four singles players eliminated from the competition are Sabalenka (2), Coco Gauff (4), Karolina Muchova (7) and Marta Kostyuk (9) who replaced top seed Elena Rybakina who withdrew with an illness before the event started. Saturday's WTA Finals semifinals are all set as it will be Svitolina vs. Noskova and Pegula vs. Andreeva. Svitolina frustrated Sabalenka, who won the BNP Paribas Open at the Indian Wells Tennis Garden in March, early in Friday's match. After falling behind 2-0, Svitolina got on a roll, winning six of the last seven games to take the first set 6-3. But that momentum was short-lived as Sabalenka started to find her form in the second set, comfortably taking it 6-3 and then breaking Svitolina to start the third set, punctuated with a roar and a fist pump for the former World No. 1. Undaunted, though, the veteran Svitolina broke right back to even the third set and reapply the pressure to Sabalenka. Svitolina then held serve and broke Sabalenka again to take a 3-1 lead. The three-game burst had Sabalenka talking to herself, hitting the court with her racket and looking to the heavens. The body language told the story as the cool and calm Svitolina finished off the match from that point on, collecting an impressive victory over a player that has flummoxed her over the years. The win is another part of a stellar on-court year for Svitolina, who has won twice (Auckland and Rome) and moved back into the top 10. The players and fans have become used to it by now, but matches between Ukrainian players and Russian or Belarusian players — like Friday's Svitolina-Sabalenka matchup — still come with an extra layer of procedural differences due to the ongoing war in the Ukraine. The two players do not shake hands before or after the match. A pre-match photo which is usually taken with the chair umpire and both players is not taken together as each player indiv

item.title: On Kirk Cousins (and Packers Week, Too!)
item.description: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - SEPTEMBER 13: Kirk Cousins #8 of the Minnesota Vikings passes the ball in the second quarter of the game against the Green Bay Packers at U.S. Bank Stadium on September 13, 2020 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Kirk Cousins is once again the quarterback for the Minnesota Vikings. Welcome to the most exciting, if anxiety-riddled, stretch of Vikings football in memory. The next few months will be unlike any other. General manager Nolan Teasley did what he had to do. A 3rd-round pick was a small price to pay to avoid the iceberg. After an embarrassing, mind-boggling, inept offensive showing in front of the entire nation on Monday Night Football that threatened a full-on locker room mutiny and the season’s implosion, the ship has now been steered into calmer waters. Whether it will be there when the calendar turns to January is still very much up in the air. The only situations even remotely comparable were Sam Bradford’s arrival days before the 2016 season and Randy Moss’ return in 2010. While the former started well, defeating the Green Bay Packers in Week 1, it ultimately petered out. The latter didn’t even get that far. Let’s hope for better luck this time around. NARRATIVES, NARRATIVES EVERYWHERE! Super Bowl Dreams Are Back On. Through nine games as the Raiders’ starter, with offensive weapons no one would confuse with the 1999 Rams, Kirk Cousins was on pace for more TD passes (38) than he had with the Vikings (2021 and 2022) after the NFL moved to a 17-game regular season. He would just fall short of the passing yardage he had in 2022 (4,547). In an earlier article, I noted that a torn Achilles in a quarterback’s plant leg is the worst non-throwing-arm injury you can sustain. Recovery is challenging and often takes more than one season before you start to look like yourself again. I think that may explain much of what’s going on with Daniel Jones in Indy right now. Given his performance this year, there is a persuasive argument that the nature of the injury, not necessarily age, may explain the inconsistency Cousins experienced during his stint with the Atlanta Falcons. Would he have played better if he were 25? Probably. But his play for the Raiders has been a pleasant surprise that no one envisioned before the season: 2nd in passing TDs, 5th in yards, 9th in EPA per dropback, etc. All Cousins needs to do is be good. That’s it. The Raiders are 8th in points per game (26.4). We won’t even need that 95% of the time. We’d be 8-0 right now. The reason the Silver and Black are 4-5 is that their defense is last in points allowed (29.8) and yards allowed (385.4). They’re basically the 2020-21 Vikings. Under Brian Flores, we’re 1st and 2nd in those categories, respectively. The NFC is wide open right now. No one is convincing me that there is a team we can’t beat, with Cousins back throwing to Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison, and T.J. Hockenson again, and Flores’ defense as the ultima

item.title: Jonathan Taylor Says Trade Talks Are Above His Pay Grade
item.description: Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor (28) waves to fans as he leaves the field Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026, after losing a game against the Dallas Cowboys at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Despite intense speculation connecting them to Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor, the New York Giants made no moves by the NFL trade deadline. Per reports, while a second-round and a fifth-round pick were reportedly offered, the transaction failed to complete before the deadline arrived. As a 2-7 Indianapolis Colts member, Taylor stayed put and expressed his views clearly during his initial media session after the deadline expired. Taylor Takes The High Road Speaking with reporters, Taylor was blunt when asked about not getting traded to a contender like the Giants. He told the media that trade decisions are way above his pay grade and that he is glad he does not have to make those hard calls. Taylor stated that his only job is to come in and make sure he is at his best each and every single day for his coaches and teammates. He told reporters, according to Heavy.com , “I would hate to be in that situation. But I know that they have a vision and a plan for it.” While Giants fans might have wanted a blockbuster move, Taylor seems content to just execute the plan the Colts have set out for him right now. He emphasized that the best thing to help the team is executing and getting a win versus Miami. Why The Colts Held Firm It is easy to wonder why the Colts did not trade their best remaining player when they are sitting at 2-7 and have no first-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. ESPN’s Dan Graziano stated that Indianapolis felt no urgency to trade since Taylor is signed through the 2028 season. The front office clearly decided that keeping their star running back was more valuable than the premium picks they could have gotten in return. Several weeks prior, the Colts traded Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner, and on Tuesday they also parted ways with wide receivers Keenan Allen and Josh Downs. Unlike other key departures, Taylor was not moved, and he never asked for a trade or stated a desire to leave. This silence suggests he is willing to ride it out in Indy while the team rebuilds around him. Giants Find Value Elsewhere The Giants missed out on the biggest name at the deadline, but they did not mortgage their future for an overpriced player. GM Joe Schoen stood pat because the asking prices for defensive tackles were too steep and the team only has five picks in the 2027 draft. Rather than exchanging picks, the organization noted that rookie defensive lineman Bobby Jamison-Travis has gained more playing time and recorded a 77.5 run‑defense grade versus the Texans, per reports.

item.title: SpaceX launches Starship on ambitious 22-hour Flight 15 test, but aborts booster 'chopsticks' catch (video)
item.description: null STARBASE, Texas — SpaceX launched the 15th test flight of its massive Starship rocket today (Nov. 13) and is preparing the vehicle's upper stage for its first-ever return to the launch site in less than 24 hours. Flight 15 lifted off from SpaceX 's Starbase facility here in South Texas at 5:47 p.m. ET (2247 GMT; 4:47 p.m. local Texas time). The towering Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage cleared the tower without incident and climbed into the skies under more than 18 million pounds of thrust from the booster's 33 Raptor 3 engines. The flight continued nominally through its initial ascent, with the successful execution of Super Heavy's main engine cutoff and Ship's subsequent hot-staging — firing its own Raptors during separation from the booster — about 2.5 minutes after launch. Following stage separation, Super Heavy reoriented for a planned return to Starbase as Ship powered its way toward low Earth orbit (LEO). SpaceX's Starship megarocket launches on its 15th test flight from Starbase, Texas on Nov. 13, 2026. (Image credit: Future/Josh Dinner, Space.com) SpaceX originally planned to catch Super Heavy with the Starbase launch tower's giant mechanical "chopstick" arms. But it wasn't to be: The company called off the catch attempt and brought the booster down for a controlled splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico about 6.5 minutes after launch, for reasons that were not immediately clear. A successful catch would have been a significant milestone for SpaceX and its efforts to design Starship as a fully and rapidly reusable launch vehicle. It would have been the first successful recovery of a Version 3 (V3) Super Heavy , which SpaceX began flying earlier this year. The company previously recovered three of its V1 Super Heavy vehicles and reused two of those in later flights. Starship rises into the skies above South Texas on Flight 15. (Image credit: SpaceX) Ship goes to orbit Ship's Raptors continued to fire following stage separation, completing their first burn just after eight minutes into flight. All went according to plan after that for Ship as well: A second engine burn lasting about 20 seconds parked Ship in LEO at an altitude of around 170 miles (275 kilometers) at T+26 minutes and 10 seconds. "We’ve got a nominal orbit insertion, so Starship now in orbit around Earth for the second time ever," SpaceX's Dan Huot said during today's Flight 15 launch webcast. "That’s a really great moment." Ship first reached orbit on Flight 14 , which launched on Sept. 28. Ship is carrying 26 of SpaceX's Starlink V3 spacecraft, which will be deployed into LEO today over a 42-minute span starting 35 minutes after launch, if all goes to plan. The upgraded wireless internet satellites will be the second V3 batch to reach orbit, after a set of 26 that were delivered on Flight 14 . V3s are significantly more powerful than SpaceX's V2 Starlinks, which currently number more than 11,000 in LEO. The addition of this new set of V3s will add a terabit of data

item.title: FAA orders third nationwide ground stop in its history
item.description: On Friday afternoon, days after expanding use of an AI tool , the Federal Aviation Administration issued a nationwide ground stop, halting departures from all US airports. Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy announced the ground stop on X , citing a "communication issue impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers." Duffy promised updates as more information is known and said FAA staff were troubleshooting the problem. Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said that the ground stop was not prompted by a security threat. "This is a telecommunications outage out of the FAA. Out of an abundance of caution, we have grounded all of the flights," Mullin said . "There's no indication as of yet that this is a nefarious attack against us." Mullin said the FAA would handle incoming international flights on a case-by-case basis. Read full article Comments

item.title: US says forces responded to suspected drone activity over base in Britain
item.description: US forces responded to possible unauthorized drone activity over a military base in Britain on Friday, a US Air Force spokesperson said, in the latest security incident at a facility hosting American military aircraft. “No personnel, aircraft or infrastructure were affected” at the RAF Lakenheath base, the Air Force spokesperson said in a statement. “We continue to work closely with our host nation counterparts to ensure the safety and security of our US service members, US and host nation civilians, contractors, and all of our families,” the statement added. Nick Timothy, a local member of parliament, said in a statement on Facebook that he had been in touch with authorities at the base and was “told there is no threat to the public, and the incident is now resolved.” A post on the official RAF Lakenheath Facebook page earlier this week urged people to report “suspicious activity, including unauthorized drone activity.” “Our strongest security asset is an observant community,” the post said. The possible drone incident at Lakenheath came after the US Justice Department announced charges earlier in the week against three men it described as “Iranian operatives” over their role in an alleged terrorist plot at RAF Fairford, another British base. The three men allegedly helped plan and direct the September incident at the base, which came to light when police were called after a local farmer reported seeing a group of men with several white vans engaged in “suspicious” activity. – Iran war fallout – A US charging document stated that a man identified as Mohammad Ali al-Hassani directed unnamed individuals to drive to the base in the vans, some of which contained barrels of fuel, and that he earlier paid the group to buy metallic objects that could be used as shrapnel. Days later, the United States withdrew all its B-1 bombers from the base. UK police last month charged two British men with national security offenses related to the RAF Fairford incident. One was charged with assisting a foreign intelligence service, believed to be in Iran, and another with entering a prohibited place for a purpose “prejudicial” to the UK. Flight-tracking data showed Tuesday that the US military had removed at least a dozen aircraft from another British airbase, RAF Mildenhall, following what the Wall Street Journal said was a threat from Iran. The United States has flown military aircraft from bases in Britain as part of the US-Israeli war against Iran sparked earlier this year, which saw Tehran respond by launching missiles and drones at countries across the region, while the militant groups it backs also entered the fray. In an interview broadcast Wednesday, Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei threatened to strike US bases beyond the Middle East, including in Europe, if they are used for attacks against the Islamic republic. item.title: Millions of Americans are not taking their GLP-1 drugs as prescribed
item.description: GLP-1 medications are everywhere these days. The peptide-based drugs are both highly effective and wildly popular for diabetes, weight loss and a growing range of connected chronic health conditions, including cardiovascular disease and obstructive sleep apnea. But, amid the boom, the latest data suggests millions of Americans have turned to unapproved versions and are using the potent drugs in ways doctors never intended, raising questions about what that real-world use means for safety and efficacy. In a study published this week , researchers at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention broke down survey data of GLP-1 use collected between July and August of 2025. Based on responses from over 8,000 US adults, the researchers estimate that about one in 10 US adults (9.8 percent) used a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist, aka GLP-1 medication, in 2025. That's around 27 million adults. The study was published in the CDC's Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report. Among GLP-1 users, nearly half (44 percent) reported using their GLP-1 in a way that was different from how it was prescribed. Users skipped doses, delayed getting refills, and used smaller doses than prescribed, among other changes. More than half of the people modifying how they used the drug said the changes were because of cost or availability reasons. Cost and access barriers were most pronounced among younger GLP-1 users. Fifty-eight percent of adults 14­–39 years old who modified their use cited cost as a barrier, compared with just 20 percent of adults 65 or older who said the same. Read full article Comments

item.title: Who Gets To Compete?
item.description: Opposition talks are continuing. Campaigns are gathering pace. But access, legal certainty and confidence in the vote are becoming defining questions of the election. In Yelwata, Peter Obi stood before a community carrying the wounds of mass violence. In Akure, the APC called its organisation to work for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election. In London, INEC’s chairman faced questions about whether Nigerians could trust the coming vote. These were different settings for the same election. Together, they reveal a contest in which persuading voters is only part of the task. Candidates must sustain their organisations, establish their right to participate and reach citizens safely. The electoral commission must demonstrate that those citizens’ choices will be recorded faithfully. The week’s developments sharpen a fundamental question: how open, credible and competitive will the road to 2027 remain? Lagos Raises the Stakes Thursday’s reported attack on an NDC town hall gathering in Oregun, Lagos, deserves particular attention. According to reporting from the scene, armed men disrupted the gathering, participants were injured and a suspect was arrested. The NDC alleged political responsibility; the Lagos APC denied sponsoring the incident. The report established no independent evidence linking the attackers to a political party. Investigation must establish who acted, who organised them and whether anyone provided support. The democratic principle requires no such delay: citizens must be able to attend lawful political meetings without fearing assault. Violence can influence an election before a ballot is cast. It can discourage attendance, make venues reluctant to host meetings, increase campaign costs and persuade volunteers to stay home. Its effects therefore extend beyond the immediate victims. When intimidation restricts participation, it changes the conditions under which candidates compete. Political leaders should condemn attacks consistently, including when the victims support their opponents. Security agencies must provide protection on the same basis. Makinde Keeps the Alliance Door Open Seyi Makinde’s latest comments give fresh substance to the opposition’s continuing conversation about cooperation. In an interview reported today, the Oyo governor confirmed active discussions involving Atiku Abubakar and Peter Obi. He said decisions should draw on evidence, manifestos, previous performance and public sentiment. He did not announce an agreement or endorse a preferred candidate. That distinction separates a development worth watching from a coalition already formed. The negotiations face a familiar practical difficulty: cooperation requires choices that impose costs on participants. Someone may need to surrender an ambition, accept another candidate’s leadership or persuade supporters to work with former rivals. An agreement also needs to travel beyond the negotiating room. item.title: Global outage: Microsoft blames network change for service disruption
item.description: …Apologises to customers By Juliet Umeh The US-based technology, Microsoft, has blamed a recent network change for a global outage that disrupted its workplace services, including Outlook, Teams and Copilot. While apologising to its customers in a statement, the company said the incident stemmed from an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced after a subsequent network change. The statement reads: “The incident was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change.” The outage affected customers and partners in different regions, disrupting access to Microsoft services. The company said it had addressed the underlying issue and was continuing to restore services to remaining customers and regions. “We are seeing broad recovery and stability across our services,” it said, adding that the disruption was “not related to cyber or AI/agents.” Microsoft said services were restored gradually because of the scale of demand. “Given the scale of demand, we restored services gradually, validating stability at each stage. While this took longer, it helped ensure a stable restoration. “We are deeply sorry for the disruption this incident has caused our customers and partners,” it said. Microsoft added that it would release a full post-incident report after completing its review of the outage. The disruption affected organisations that rely on Microsoft’s workplace tools, with reports of interruptions to services in sectors including healthcare, aviation, policing and education. item.title: Silva says Portugal ready for spotlight without Ronaldo
item.description: Portugal midfielder Bernardo Silva said Friday his team could cope with any extra pressure on them following Cristiano Ronaldo’s international retirement, ahead of their first match without the superstar forward. Jorge Jesus’s side host Denmark in Braga on Saturday in the Nations League, with a tribute planned for their all-time leading goalscorer. Real Madrid’s Silva, who inherits the captain’s armband from Ronaldo, admitted that the striker had been the main focus for much of the past two decades but backed the team to cope with the pressure in the 41-year-old’s absence. “Everyone knows the weight Cristiano carries. Most people went to the stadium to see Cristiano, many went just for him, and that’s not going to happen now,” Silva told reporters. “The national team players are used to the spotlight, the pressure, and the responsibility, as well as being pointed at when things don’t go well — so that’s not an issue.” Portugal will pay tribute to five-time Ballon d’Or winner Ronaldo before the game against Denmark, with media reporting the squad will walk out wearing number seven jerseys, Ronaldo’s number. Whether Ronaldo will be present is unknown, after he fell out with veteran coach Jorge Jesus in September. Last week Ronaldo said he was bringing down the curtain on his storied international career. Ronaldo made his debut for Portugal in 2003 and went on to play a world record 234 times for his country, scoring 146 goals. “Nobody can forget Cris’s 23 years in the national team and everything he did,” Jesus told reporters. “I think (paying tribute) is a brilliant idea to continue to remind us that he is a legend of Portuguese football.” Portugal have already sealed qualification to the quarter-finals of the Nations League, winning all four matches in Group A4. The post Silva says Portugal ready for spotlight without Ronaldo appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: On this day in space! Nov. 13, 1971: NASA's Mariner 9 becomes 1st spacecraft to orbit Mars, revealing close looks at the Martian surface
item.description: null On Nov. 13, 1971, Mariner 9 became the first spacecraft to orbit Mars. At the time, scientists didn't know much about the Red Planet. NASA had several Mars flybys before Mariner 9 . Those flybys showed that Mars had a cratered surface , so some scientists thought that Mars looked just like the moon. Then Mariner 9 blew blew their minds. When Mariner 9 got to Mars , it arrived in the middle of a dust storm. It saw some tall structures sticking through the clouds. When the dust settled, images from Mariner 9 revealed that these structures were the tops of huge volcanoes. One volcano, Olympus Mons , is the tallest in the solar system. Mariner 9 also spotted an enormous canyon called Valles Marineris . This canyon is five times longer than the Grand Canyon in Arizona. Mariner 9 worked for one year in orbit. When it ran out of gas, NASA shut it off. But the spacecraft remains one of the most famous Mars voyagers of all time. The Mariner 9 spacecraft, seen here in a NASA model, was the first to orbit Mars in 1971. (Image credit: NASA) Here's why it mattered Mariner 9 cemented its place in space history when it entered into orbit around Mars, the first human-built spacecraft ever to do so. The NASA spacecraft actually beat the Soviet Union's own Mars 2 spacecraft to the Red Planet, even though Mars 2 "had an 11-day head start," NASA said in a mission description . (Mars 2 would go on to be the first human-built craft to impact the surface of Mars when it crashed into the Red Planet.) But it was the science from Mariner 9 that transformed Mars from a mysterious Red Planet into a full world for humans to explore. The Boldest Mars Missions in History The Mariner 9 mission first saw the peak of Olympus Mons on Mars in the midst of a global dust storm in 1971. (Image credit: NASA/JPL) Mariner 9 carried four primary instruments to study Mars, including a camera system for imaging, an ultraviolet spectrometer, an infrared spectrometer and an infrared radiometer. The probe mapped 85% of Mars with those tools during its nearly one-year mission. The Mariner 9 spacecraft discovered 20 giant volcanoes on Mars (including Olympus Mars) and made key observations to map Valles Marineris, which runs 2,500 miles (4,000 kilometers) long acros the Tharsis region and is 120 miles (200 km) wide. "The canyon was named in honor of Mariner 9," NASA said in an overview . In all, Mariner 9 took 7,329 photos of the surface of Mars, mapping the planet down to a resolution of between 1/2-1 mile (1-2 km). It also snapped at least 80 photos of Phobos and Deimos, the two small moons of Mars. By February 1972, Mariner 9's supply of gaseous nitrogen, which it used to feed its attitide control thrusters, had run dry. NASA finally shut down the mission in October 1972. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

item.title: FAA expands AI advice to manage air traffic congestion across entire US airspace
item.description: The US government has expanded the use of an AI tool for advising air traffic controllers to assist in managing air traffic across the entire national airspace system. Airline executives have voiced support for the rollout, but the US labor union representing air traffic controllers has said it was not involved in designing or testing the AI-driven system. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) says the $875 million SMART system has helped reroute 180 flights since being implemented in airspace over Washington, DC, on September 21. The agency claims that this saved an average of 10 minutes per flight and almost 80 gallons of fuel per flight—and it is apparently hoping such results can be replicated nationwide through the expanded deployment. “After a successful initial rollout to the National Capital Region in September, the FAA will now use SMART in the airspace of all 22 centers across the country to reduce delays, reduce fuel consumption and improve the travel experience for the flying public,” according to the agency statement posted on November 10. item.title: Chinese AI labs are training models on Nvidia's Blackwell despite export controls, says ex-OpenAI engineer
item.description: US export controls are not stopping AI labs in China from using restricted Nvidia chips, according to a report from a former OpenAI engineer. Will DePue, who left the AI giant earlier this year to launch Unemployment Labs, an AI research consultancy, published forensic evidence showing that "DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax and Ant Group have gained access to Nvidia's Blackwell GPUs, despite restrictions on exporting these chips to China, and are using that hardware to create their AI models." "This sounds insane, but I discovered that almost every AI model carries a hidden signature of the GPU that trained it," said DePue in a social media post . "When a model is first set up, the starting values of its weights are laid out in a pattern that depends on the exact GPU. Each combination of GPU and seed number produces a unique pattern – a sort of fingerprint of the hardware used to create the model. Traces of that pattern survive training into the published model." It doesn't sound that insane. The resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang followed from revelations that he had an affair with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, who, in 2023, founded Singapore-based Megaspeed International. That company is reportedly under investigation by US authorities for allegedly smuggling Nvidia chips to China. Huang's departure coincides with a renewed push to tighten US chip export controls. House Speaker Mike Johnson supports the idea . And there are at least four bills awaiting consideration that aim to limit China's access to leading edge AI tech: the AI Overwatch Act, the Chip Security Act, Match Act, and the Cloud Security Act. On Monday, US Senators Jim Banks (R-Ind.) and Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) cited Jensen Huang's "relationship with a suspected Chinese spy" as a justification for passing the AI Overwatch Act, which would codify the Trump administration's existing chip export controls. The Trump administration on Thursday said it's not sure whether Alice Huang was a spy, an allegation denied by Beijing and currently under investigation by the FBI. Whatever the case, the current rules clearly are not working. Only a few weeks ago, Lava, an Israel-based security company, said it had found "32 Nvidia B300 GPUs, part of Nvidia's Blackwell Ultra generation, through publicly exposed monitoring endpoints with IP addresses geolocated to China." These GPUs, Lava noted, are subject to US export controls [PDF]. The security biz said its findings followed from the exposure of monitoring systems intended for internal infrastructure management that were publicly exposed. How DePue reached his conclusion The analysis published through DePue's consultancy, "Top Chinese Frontier AI Models Carry the Fingerprint of Export-Controlled Nvidia Blackwell GPUs," takes a different approach: analyzing the published weights of various models from Chinese AI labs.
