item.title: FG records 16 Nigerian deaths in Addis Ababa, warns travellers
item.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja The Federal Government has warned Nigerians, particularly those with pre-existing medical conditions, to exercise caution when travelling through Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, following the deaths of 16 Nigerians in the city this year. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs disclosed this in a travel advisory issued on Friday, stating that the deaths recorded by Nigeria’s Diplomatic Mission in Addis Ababa were reportedly linked to health complications associated with the city’s high altitude. The ministry explained that Addis Ababa is situated approximately 2,355 metres (7,726 feet) above sea level, where lower atmospheric pressure results in reduced oxygen availability. It noted that the conditions could pose increased health risks to travellers with certain underlying medical conditions, particularly cardiovascular and respiratory ailments. According to the advisory, although healthy individuals are generally able to adapt to reduced oxygen levels in high-altitude environments, people with certain pre-existing health conditions may experience complications. The Federal Government therefore advised Nigerians whose medical conditions could be worsened by high altitudes to seek appropriate medical advice before undertaking journeys involving transit through the Ethiopian capital. It also urged travellers with underlying medical conditions to consult medical professionals and obtain necessary guidance before embarking on their trips. The ministry, however, clarified that the advisory was not intended to discourage Nigerians from travelling to or transiting through Addis Ababa. Rather, it said the notice was aimed at ensuring that medically vulnerable travellers were adequately informed about the possible effects of high altitudes and took necessary precautions. The advisory stated, “This year, Nigeria’s Diplomatic Mission in Addis Ababa has recorded 16 deaths involving Nigerians transiting through the city, reportedly linked to health complications associated with high altitudes. “While healthy individuals are generally able to adapt to reduced oxygen levels in high-altitude environments, persons with certain pre-existing medical ailments, particularly cardiovascular and respiratory conditions, may experience increased health risks in such conditions. “In view of the foregoing, Nigerians with pre-existing health conditions that can be exacerbated by high altitudes are strongly advised to exercise caution when planning journeys that involve transit through Addis Ababa. “Travellers with underlying medical conditions are also urged to obtain appropriate medical guidance before undertaking such journeys.” The ministry reiterated that the advisory was not intended to discourage Nigerians from travelling to or transiting through Addis Ababa but to ensure that those vulnerable to the physiological effects of high altitudes were adequately informed. item.title: Goalkeeper Owono suspended for 12 matches after De Miguel death
item.description: FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono was suspended for 12 matches by the Spanish football federation’s disciplinary committee on Friday after his challenge on Jesus de Miguel resulted in the death of the Tenerife striker last week. Equatorial Guinea international Owono was sent off in the second division clash on November 2 after racing into midfield and colliding with De Miguel while trying to clear an aerial ball. After the collision De Miguel, 30, was placed in intensive care in hospital and the Spanish forward died on November 3. “The assessment of the conduct under consideration in these proceedings must be based on the facts expressly recorded in the referee’s report, which states that the player was sent off for ‘violently striking an opponent in the chest with his leg, using excessive force, while the ball was in play’,” said the committee in a statement. “The tragic outcome of the incident, resulting in the death of Jesus de Miguel Alameda, is public knowledge. “In view of the nature of the conduct described and the accompanying circumstances… the maximum sanction, 12 matches of suspension, is justified.” Spanish police sources last week told AFP an investigation into what happened had been opened under judicial supervision. Owono said he was enduring the “hardest days of my life” after De Miguel’s death. “These are the hardest days of my life. I struggle to find the words and it is very difficult for me to process anything that has happened,” said Owono in a statement published by his club Andorra last week. “I feel immense pain over the loss of Jesus. I think of him, of his family, and of all the people who loved him. “I know there will be many issues to address, and I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect. But right now, honestly, I cannot think about anything other than Jesus and the pain we are going through. Rest in peace, Jesus.” FC Andorra coach Carles Manso said Thursday it would be Owono who decides if and when he returns to football after the tragic incident. On Saturday Tenerife fans and players gathered at the club’s stadium for a memorial and farewell to De Miguel. His funeral took place last Thursday and around 400 mourners attended, including Spain coach Luis de la Fuente and Real Madrid president Florentino Perez. item.title: Cities: Skylines' Best Replacement Is Finally Here and Better than Expected
item.description: 2026 is the year I got massively into city builders, and by massively I mean I played Cities: Skylines more than anything else for the first half of the year. I started dabbling with city builder-slash-logistics games in the second half of the year, like Anno 117 , and turned my attention to Transport Fever 3 soon after. When I first learned about Transport Fever 3 , I called it "like" Cities: Skylines . It looked a lot like a traditional city builder, albeit one where you focus on roads more than zoning. After playing it over the last month or so, though, I realize the difference between city builder and logistics planner is a lot more distinct than I initially gave it credit for — and I've irreversibly become a logistics sicko.

item.title: 60 years ago the Leonid meteor shower produced 144,000 meteors per hour. Could it happen again?
item.description: null This year marks a rather auspicious anniversary for meteor watchers. Sixty years ago , one of the most stupendous Leonid meteor displays lit up the predawn skies over the central and western U.S. So, what will the 2026 Leonids bring us? And what might they bring in the years to come? The Leonid meteor shower is one of the most celebrated of the year's annual displays of "shooting stars." The mere mention of the Leonids usually elicits mental images of a sky filled with shooting stars pouring down through the sky like rain. Such meteor storms have indeed occurred with the Leonids, such as in 1833 and 1966 when meteor rates of tens of thousands per hour were observed. In more recent years, most notably 1999 , 2001 and 2002 , lesser Leonid displays of up to "only" a few thousand meteors per hour took place. Unfortunately, that's not likely to be the case this year. In fact, comparatively speaking, this is going to be a lean year for the Leonids chiefly because of the expected lack of any significant activity. Although the Leonids are one of the most famous of all the annual meteor displays, this year they're not likely to be very productive. It's probable they are going to be rather weak and there probably will be long stretches when not a single Leonid will be seen. I'll explain why in a moment. First, let's find out about this shower's lineage. What causes the Leonids? The Leonids are so named because the shower's radiant point, from where the meteors seem to fan out, is located within the constellation of Leo the Lion, from the backward question mark pattern of stars known as " The Sickle." The meteors are caused by the Tempel-Tuttle comet , which sweeps through the inner solar system every 33⅓ years. Each time the comet passes closest to the sun it leaves a "river of rubble" in its wake: a dense trail of dusty debris. A meteor storm becomes possible if the Earth were to score a direct hit on a fresh dust trail ejected by the comet over the past several centuries. The "lion's share" (no pun intended) of comet dust can be found just ahead and trailing behind Tempel-Tuttle. That comet last swept through the inner solar system in 1998. That's why spectacular meteor showers were seen in 1999, 2001 and 2002, with declining numbers thereafter. The most famous depiction of the 1833 Leonids, actually produced in 1888 for the Adventist book Bible Readings for the Home Circle . The engraving is by Adolf Vollmy based upon an original painting by the Swiss artist Karl Jauslin, that is in turn based on a first-person account of the 1833 storm by a minister, Joseph Harvey Waggoner on his way from Florida to New Orleans. (Image credit: Adolf Vollmy - Bible Readings for the Home Circle. Public Domain) When is the best time to look for Leonids? item.title: Tinubu Hails Bakassi Seaport, Says Project Will Create Jobs, Boost Trade
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has described the groundbreaking of the Bakassi Deep Seaport in Cross River State as a major milestone in Nigeria’s economic diversification, saying the project will open new commercial corridors, stimulate industrialisation and create jobs. Represented by Vice President Kashim Shettima at the ceremony in Bakassi on Friday, November 13, 2026, Tinubu commended Governor Bassey Otu and the people of Cross River for sustaining the project’s vision and moving it towards actualisation. The President recalled that the project was conceived in 2014, with an Environmental and Social Impact Assessment developed in March 2015, before receiving fresh impetus under Otu. Designed with a 20-metre draft, the port is expected to accommodate large vessels that currently bypass Nigerian ports. It is also linked to a 260-kilometre superhighway intended to facilitate the movement of cargo to markets across the country. Tinubu credited Otu’s determination with helping to overcome institutional and financial challenges, including efforts to secure a $3.5 billion financing arrangement with Afreximbank and formalise the Public-Private Partnership framework in February 2025. “This is beyond a Cross River dream. It is a Nigerian project. It is a poverty breaker,” he said. President Kashim Shettima at the ceremony in Bakassi on Friday Tinubu stressed that the Bakassi port would complement, rather than compete with, Lagos, which handles more than 80 per cent of Nigeria’s foreign trade. “Lagos is not our enemy. Lagos is our elder brother in trade. No country eats with one hand. No country carries all its loads on one shoulder. That shoulder will break,” he said. He argued that establishing another major maritime gateway would reduce pressure on Lagos ports, ease congestion and lower costs. “When Calabar works, Nigeria works on two legs,” the President added. He said Nigeria had not fully exploited its coastline along the Gulf of Guinea, while neighbouring countries continued to benefit from trade that could be attracted to Nigerian ports. Tinubu said the Bakassi project would help retain regional cargo, expand access to international markets and strengthen Nigeria’s competitiveness in maritime trade. He noted that about 90 per cent of cargo moves by sea, but Nigeria handles only a fraction of regional cargo trade despite its economic position in West Africa. The port, he said, would help close the gap, reduce dependence on a single maritime gateway and enable the country to capture a larger share of regional commerce. Shettima and Governor Otu at the groundbreaking event. The President also acknowledged the territorial and economic losses suffered by Cross River following the Bakassi Peninsula ruling and the loss of oil revenue. He, however, said the setbacks had not diminished the people’s courage, hospitality and resilience. “The peninsula was not the end of your story, but the beginning of your next chapter,” he said, urging residents to protect the p

item.title: Lagos NDC meeting attack threatens democracy — APM candidate
item.description: By Dapo Akinrefon The governorship candidate of the Action Peoples Movement (APM) in Lagos State, Prince Laja Adeoye, has condemned the attack on supporters of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) during their town hall meeting in Lagos, describing the incident as shameful and a threat to democracy. Adeoye said the disruption of the meeting at Classique Event Centre, Oregun, Ikeja, on Thursday, amounted to an infringement on the constitutional rights of citizens to assemble and freely express their political views. He warned that the use of thugs to disrupt opposition gatherings could heighten political tension ahead of the 2027 general elections. Adeoye said, “Nobody should be attacked for supporting a candidate of his or her choice. What happened in Lagos on Thursday was shameful and unacceptable in a democracy.” He described the incident as particularly disturbing, noting that Lagos had traditionally been regarded as a centre of political activities where parties and candidates could canvass for support. According to him, the attack was not merely against the NDC but also against the democratic process and Nigerians who believe in free and fair elections. The APM candidate urged the Lagos State Police Command to identify, arrest and prosecute those responsible for the incident, irrespective of their political affiliation or status. He warned that failure to bring the perpetrators to justice could encourage similar attacks in other parts of the country as political activities gather momentum ahead of the 2027 elections. Adeoye also expressed concern over the safety of voters, candidates and journalists during the campaign period, recalling reports that a journalist covering the meeting was attacked and dispossessed of his working equipment. He called on political leaders to rise above partisan interests and condemn violence, stressing that democracy could not thrive in an atmosphere of fear and intimidation. The APM candidate commended the NDC supporters for maintaining their composure despite the alleged provocation, saying their conduct demonstrated commitment to democratic values. “The supporters did not retaliate. They conducted themselves in a peaceful manner. That is the spirit we need to sustain our democracy,” he said. He urged political parties to caution their supporters against violence and embrace issue-based campaigns rather than intimidation and thuggery. Adeoye also called on the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), security agencies and other political stakeholders to work together to guarantee a level playing field for all parties ahead of the 2027 elections. He said Lagos, as the country’s commercial nerve centre, should demonstrate that elections could be contested and won without violence. He further urged the National Peace Committee and civil society organisations to intervene by encouraging political actors to embrace peaceful political engagement. According to him, Nigerians were more concerned about findin

item.title: Nasarawa pensioners begin enforcement of ₦4bn court order
item.description: By Edwin Philip, Lafia A group of 601 retired civil servants in Nasarawa State has commenced enforcement of a court order directing the recovery of over ₦4 billion in outstanding gratuities and other entitlements owed them by the state government. The pensioners, under the aegis of the Concerned Group of Nasarawa State Pensioners, secured a consent judgment against the state government in 2020 over the alleged non-payment of their retirement benefits. Their spokespersons, Mr Simon Auna and Mallam Usman Adamu, disclosed the development while speaking with journalists in Lafia on Friday. The group said it subsequently obtained an order from the National Industrial Court, Makurdi, awarding 25 per cent post-judgment interest on the judgment sum, bringing the total amount being sought to over ₦4 billion. According to the pensioners, following the alleged failure of the state government to comply with the judgment, their lawyers approached the Senior District Court in Makurdi, presided over by Justice Ada Jack. The court subsequently directed six commercial banks to release funds belonging to the Nasarawa State Government, amounting to over ₦4 billion, for payment to the affected retirees. In a move to enforce the order, the pensioners’ legal team, accompanied by court bailiffs, visited some branches of one of the commercial banks in Makurdi, Benue State, where they removed some movable properties. Speaking on the development, counsel to the pensioners, Mrs Doofan Sefa-Aii, said the legal team would continue to operate within the law to ensure full recovery of the funds owed the retirees. Another counsel, Mr Awo Matthew, appealed to the Nasarawa State Government and the banks involved to allow the legal process to take its course, considering the hardship the pensioners had endured while pursuing payment of their entitlements. However, the Director of Corporate Services and Arbitration at the Nasarawa State Ministry of Justice, Mr Usman Aliyu, said the state government had taken all necessary legal steps, including filing a motion for a stay of execution of the court order. Meanwhile, Adamu, who is the group’s Lafia Local Government Chairman, and Auna, its Legal Adviser, described the court order as a significant breakthrough after years of seeking payment of their entitlements. They said the development had renewed their hope of recovering the outstanding benefits. The pensioners reaffirmed their determination to pursue their entitlements through lawful means until the matter was resolved. item.title: Zulum offers soldiers N50,000 each, logistics for Borno deployment
item.description: By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri Borno State Governor, Professor Babagana Umara Zulum, has announced a ₦50,000 welfare support for each soldier preparing for deployment to Maiwa and Koshebe communities in the state, alongside a pledge to provide operational logistics to strengthen security. Zulum gave the assurance on Friday during a visit to the headquarters of the 24 Task Force Brigade in Dikwa Local Government Area, where he met with the Brigade Commander, Brigadier General Aminu Gumel. The governor said the visit was aimed at exploring measures to improve security along the Maiduguri–Mafa–Dikwa–Ngala highway, a strategic economic corridor linking several communities in eastern Borno State. He noted that the highway was vital to trade, transportation and cross-border commercial activities, stressing that improved security would enable residents to travel safely, move agricultural produce and rebuild their livelihoods. “My visit is primarily aimed at exploring measures to strengthen security along the strategic economic corridor, which connects Maiduguri to several communities in eastern Borno and serves as a vital route for trade, transportation and cross-border commercial activities,” Zulum said. Addressing troops preparing for deployment to Maiwa and Koshebe, the governor pledged to provide operational logistics and sustained welfare support. He also announced a payment of ₦50,000 to each soldier preparing for the deployment to the two communities. Koshebe has previously suffered deadly attacks by suspected Boko Haram insurgents. On November 28, 2020, insurgents attacked rice farmers working in fields around the community, killing more than 100 people, many of whom were seasonal farm labourers from Sokoto State. Similarly, in November 2023, suspected insurgents attacked farmers harvesting rice in the Karkut and Koshebe areas of Mafa Local Government Area, killing at least 13 people, while others were reported missing. Zulum’s administration has continued to provide logistics and welfare assistance to security agencies as part of efforts to support military operations, improve security and facilitate the return of displaced residents to their communities. The governor was accompanied on the visit by the member representing Monguno/Nganzai/Marte Federal Constituency in the House of Representatives, Engr. Bukar Talba; member representing Dikwa Constituency in the Borno State House of Assembly, Mohammed Zakariya; Commissioner for Information and Internal Security, Professor Usman Tar; Commissioner for Local Government and Emirate Affairs, Sugun Mai Mele; and other senior government officials. The post Zulum offers soldiers N50,000 each, logistics for Borno deployment appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: COVID-19 loans must be repaid, NIRSAL MFB insists
item.description: By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief NIRSAL Microfinance Bank (NMFB) has clarified that the COVID-19 Targeted Credit Facility (TCF) was an intervention loan, not a grant, stressing that beneficiaries are obligated to repay the funds. The bank said deductions from the accounts of beneficiaries who accessed the facility would continue until their outstanding loans were fully liquidated, in line with the Global Standing Instruction (GSI) mechanism. In a statement issued in Abuja at the weekend, the bank explained that the GSI framework allows financial institutions to recover outstanding loan obligations from eligible accounts linked to borrowers’ Bank Verification Numbers (BVNs), subject to applicable regulatory guidelines. The bank said the clarification became necessary to address concerns surrounding loan recoveries and reassure customers and members of the public of its commitment to transparency, accountability and responsible banking practices. It explained that the COVID-19 Targeted Credit Facility was introduced by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) to support households and businesses affected by the economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. According to the bank, all beneficiaries were required to accept electronic offer letters before disbursement, with the documents clearly outlining the terms and conditions of the facility, including repayment obligations and recovery mechanisms in cases of default. “Regarding the recovery process, the Bank operates within the applicable regulatory framework, including the Global Standing Instruction (GSI) mechanism approved by the Central Bank of Nigeria,” it stated. NIRSAL MFB, however, acknowledged concerns raised by some beneficiaries over the timing and amounts of deductions, outstanding loan balances and access to repayment information. The bank said it took the complaints seriously, noting that customers must have access to accurate information about their loan accounts. It stressed that the deductions were intended to settle outstanding contractual obligations, adding that beneficiaries who disputed deductions or identified discrepancies in their repayment records should contact the bank for individual account reconciliation. “Where any beneficiary has concerns about deductions made, discrepancies in repayment records or the status of an outstanding balance, such cases should be brought to the bank’s attention for individual account reconciliation and appropriate resolution,” it said. The bank assured that legitimate complaints would be investigated and that any discrepancies established during the reconciliation process would receive the necessary attention. It urged beneficiaries seeking clarification on their loan status, repayment history or outstanding obligations to contact the bank through its officially designated customer service channels. The post COVID-19 loans must be repaid, NIRSAL MFB insists appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Customs intercepts live sea turtle at Nigeria-Benin border
item.description: By Efe Onodjae The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS), Seme Area Command, has intercepted a live endangered sea turtle allegedly being smuggled through a footpath linking Nigeria and the Republic of Benin. The Olive Ridley Sea Turtle, scientifically known as Lepidochelys olivacea, was intercepted during a routine patrol by Customs officers at about 10.30pm on Thursday, November 12, 2026. The command said the officers sighted a suspicious individual carrying a sack along the border route, but the suspect abandoned the bag and fled into a nearby bush upon noticing the patrol team. According to a statement by the command’s Public Relations Officer, Superintendent of Customs, John Tunde Ayagbalo, examination of the abandoned sack revealed the live sea turtle concealed inside. He said the animal was immediately secured and kept in safe custody before being handed over to relevant wildlife authorities for proper care, rehabilitation and eventual release into its natural habitat. The Acting Customs Area Controller, Seme Area Command, Deputy Comptroller Norman Olisah Alumanah, described the interception as a demonstration of the vigilance and professionalism of officers in tackling wildlife trafficking. Alumanah warned smugglers, poachers and their collaborators against using the nation’s borders as corridors for illegal wildlife trade, adding that the command had intensified patrols, surveillance and intelligence gathering across its area of responsibility. He also called on residents of border communities to provide credible intelligence to support the fight against wildlife trafficking. The Customs boss said the command would complement enforcement operations with stakeholder education and sensitisation on endangered species, their ecological importance and the legal implications of their unauthorised trade. Wildlife trafficking remains a major environmental crime, threatening biodiversity and the survival of endangered species through illegal exploitation for meat, eggs, shells, traditional medicine and the exotic pet trade. Nigeria is a signatory to the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES), which regulates international trade in endangered wildlife and plant species. The convention is domesticated in Nigeria through the Endangered Species (Control of International Trade and Traffic) Act, Cap E9, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria, 2004. item.title: This year’s bug count just passed 100K
item.description: Chalk up a new record for vulns. The number of Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) found and disclosed so far in 2026 surpassed 100,000 on Friday - more than double 2025’s total - and the reason can be summed up in two letters: AI. “It’s kind of wild,” Josh Bressers, VulnCheck’s director of coordinated vulnerability disclosure, told The Register . “The thing that almost scares the bejesus out of me is while 100K sounds like a lot, in a couple years we're going to say, remember when it was only 100K?” As of the time of our interview, about 4 pm UTC on Friday, VulnCheck counted 100,222 CVEs, he said. Microsoft alone added 1,094 security flaws to the total count on Tuesday, following 1,474 vulnerabilities the month before. “There's no denying the fact that vulnerability hunting with AI is driving a majority of what we're seeing.” All the major CVE Numbering Authorities (CNAs) - these are the organizations authorized by the CVE program to assign unique identifiers to security vulnerabilities - like VulnCheck, Microsoft, Oracle, GitHub, and other large enterprise IT vendors “are just screaming into the atmosphere right now,” Bressers said. “It’s AI.” Meanwhile, the percentage of these bugs that are exploited in the wild remains relatively consistent. About 1.4 percent (1,363) of the CVEs published this year have been added to VulnCheck’s Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog. “But obviously, as the number of CVEs grows, [1 percent] of 1,000 is a lot different than [1 percent] of 100,000,” Bressers said. Plus, as other security researchers have documented, the window between the public release of a security patch and attackers developing working exploits – often by reverse engineering the patch while end users are still applying the fix – is rapidly shrinking. This is also thanks to AI . From CVE to KEV From January to June, 88 percent of the exploitation observed by CrowdStrike using public proof-of-concept (PoC) code occurred within 48 hours of the code's release. The security firm said China-linked groups such as Vault Panda and Genesis Panda moved even faster, launching attacks within 24 hours of disclosure. Similarly, VulnCheck found the median time from CVE publication to exploitation falling from 120 days in 2025 to 80 days during the first half of 2026. This window has closed even further during the second half of the year, which also seems to coincide with the AI-induced vulnpocalypse . “It’s often just hours,” Bressers said, noting 14 make-me-root vulnerabilities that VulnCheck disclosed on Friday in Copeland refrigeration controllers. Two are under active exploitation. These are the devices that Iranian hackers abused to spoil food and spark fires in supermarkets across Europe . “We published those CVEs, and literally minutes later, we were seeing hits on our honey pots,” Bressers said about the Copeland device vulnerabilities. “We’ve hit a point where with anything that looks interesting, someone is taking that information a

item.title: Ebola: All 62 contacts test negative after monitoring – NCDC
item.description: By Chidinma Chukwu ABUJA — The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) has completed the 21-day monitoring of all 62 contacts linked to the imported case of Bundibugyo Virus Disease (BVD), a form of Ebola disease, confirmed in the Federal Capital Territory on October 20, 2026, with no secondary infections recorded. The Director-General of NCDC, Dr Jide Idris, disclosed this on Friday during a media briefing in Abuja, saying the last contact had been discharged from monitoring after testing negative for the virus. Idris said 13 of the 62 contacts reported fever or other non-specific symptoms during the monitoring period, but laboratory tests confirmed that none had contracted the disease. “The 21-day monitoring period for contacts linked to the index case has been completed, with the last contact discharged today. We are glad to announce that none of the contacts became ill with the disease, meaning no transmission from the index case. “A total of 62 contacts were identified, placed in quarantine and followed up by our public health teams. During the monitoring period, 13 contacts reported fever or other non-specific symptoms. All 13 were tested for Bundibugyo Virus Disease, and all tested negative,” he said. The index case was a 42-year-old Ugandan-born woman, who tested positive for the virus in Abuja on October 20. She was subsequently medically evacuated to Switzerland on October 26. Providing an update on her condition, Idris said the woman had recovered and been discharged from a hospital in Geneva. He also disclosed that seven additional suspected cases were reported and investigated in Adamawa, Rivers, Borno, Lagos and Ekiti states within the past three weeks. All seven cases tested negative for the virus. However, the NCDC chief cautioned against interpreting the completion of contact monitoring as a formal declaration that the outbreak was over. He explained that such a declaration would depend on established public health criteria and findings from continued surveillance. “It is important to note that the completion of contact monitoring does not, by itself, constitute a formal declaration that an outbreak is over. Such a determination must be based on the applicable public health criteria and the findings of ongoing surveillance. “Nigeria therefore remains vigilant, particularly given the continued occurrence of Ebola virus disease in the DRC,” he said. Idris assured Nigerians that disease surveillance and preparedness activities would continue, stressing that the agency remained committed to protecting residents and visitors. Looking ahead to the December festive season, he warned that increased travel, social interactions and large public gatherings could heighten the risk of disease transmission. He identified family celebrations, religious activities, political campaigns, concerts, festivals and sporting events as occasions likely to increase human movement and interaction. item.title: 2027: Tinubu, Atiku, Obi not there for Nigeria — Sule Lamido
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Former Jigawa State Governor and PDP chieftain, Sule Lamido, has dismissed President Bola Tinubu, former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar and former Anambra State Governor, Peter Obi, as unsuitable options for Nigeria ahead of the 2027 general election. Lamido stated this during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Friday, where he was asked which of the three political figures could attract the Northern vote in the forthcoming presidential election. Giving his assessment, the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) chieftain said none of the three contenders was in a position to address Nigeria’s challenges. He said, “Look, from my own personal opinion, in my view, voting should depend on who is the person with the right kind of quality and calibre to be able to address the same problem. Peter Obi, Tinubu, Atiku — none of them is there for Nigeria.” The former Jigawa governor also declared his support for the PDP’s presidential candidate, Professor Sandy Onor, insisting that he remained committed to the opposition party and would not vote for Tinubu in 2027. Asked whether he had endorsed Tinubu for a second term, Lamido said he remained a PDP member and would vote for his party’s candidate. He said, “I am PDP through and through. I am voting for my candidate, Professor Sandy Onor; that is my candidate. What I’m saying is that we have somebody called Professor Onor on that ballot. I’m voting him.” Lamido’s remarks come amid controversy over claims that he had endorsed Tinubu’s re-election bid after Vice-President Kashim Shettima reportedly listed him among former Jigawa governors backing the President ahead of 2027. However, the Jigawa State chapter of the PDP had earlier dismissed the claim, insisting that Lamido had neither endorsed Tinubu nor defected to the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC. item.title: NSCDC disbands anti-vandalism outpost after Gombe incident
item.description: By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe The Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), Gombe State Command, has ordered the immediate disbandment of its Anti-Vandalism Outpost following an incident involving its personnel and a truck driver in the state. The incident, which occurred on Thursday, November 12, 2026, reportedly followed a misunderstanding between personnel of the unit and a truck driver, resulting in the discharge of a firearm. The State Commandant, Commandant Muhammed Inuwa Usman, mni, also summoned all Officers-in-Charge (OCs) of the various formations and outposts to an emergency meeting on Friday to address the incident and reinforce professional standards among personnel. In a statement issued on Friday, the Command’s Public Relations Officer, Chief Superintendent of Corps Buhari Sa’ad, said the meeting was convened to address the incident and strengthen discipline and accountability within the command. During the meeting, Usman cautioned the officers against unprofessional conduct, indiscipline and actions capable of undermining the image of the Corps. He emphasised the need for personnel to remain professional, disciplined and civil, while respecting the fundamental human rights of members of the public in the discharge of their statutory responsibilities. The commandant also stressed that the use of firearms must strictly comply with established rules, operational procedures and applicable regulations, warning officers against taking the law into their own hands. As part of the disciplinary and administrative measures, he ordered the immediate disbandment of the Anti-Vandalism Outpost and directed all personnel attached to the unit to report to the State Command Headquarters without delay. Usman reiterated that the Corps would not condone indiscipline, abuse of authority or violations of citizens’ rights. He urged outpost commanders to strengthen supervision of their personnel and ensure strict adherence to the highest standards of professionalism and accountability. The commandant assured residents that the NSCDC remained committed to protecting lives and property, respecting human rights and maintaining peace and order in Gombe State. item.title: England boss Tuchel eager to end Spain’s unbeaten run
item.description: Thomas Tuchel believes England are ready to end Spain’s unbeaten record when they face the world and European champions in Madrid on Sunday. While victory offers not much more than the prospect of a more favourable Nations League quarter-final in March, it would be a landmark moment for England if they could end Spain’s run of 43 matches without defeat. “It (Spain) is a team that has forgotten how to lose, so of course it requires a top performance first of all, and if we can deliver this performance, it will give us a big boost,” said England manager Tuchel, whose side beat Croatia 2-1 at Wembley on Thursday. “I think we’re there, and I think we’re ready to win on Sunday,” the German added. “I know what it takes, and no one can ever guarantee it, but I think it’s the moment to check how far we are and to push our limit and proof of concept.” England lost the reverse fixture 3-2 at Wembley in September, but it might have been a different story had Harry Kane scored a penalty to put Tuchel’s team 3-1 up. “It’s important that we play with the same mindset that we played at home, and attack them and try to make it a physical game, and try to impose our strength.” England players have previously faced racist abuse in Spain, with Ashley Cole and Shaun Wright-Phillips targeted during a friendly in Madrid in 2004. Spain, meanwhile, must play their next home friendly with a reduced capacity as a punishment for supporters singing a discriminatory chant about Muslims during a fixture against Egypt in March. “We will never accept racism,” said Tuchel. “We will never be racist towards anyone.” He added: “I expect, of course, full support from the Spanish crowd for the Spanish team. But we will not expect anything. And I think the referee and the officials know about that… There is a protocol in place and it’s important that the players know about the protocol. “We will give our answers if stuff like this happens. Best answers are on the pitch.” The post England boss Tuchel eager to end Spain’s unbeaten run appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Meatbags suck at spotting lying LLMs, so let AI narc on itself
item.description: The internet is full of schlock, from biased news and dubious hot takes to false factoids. LogicLens aims to separate fact from fiction using the very same technology behind some of that slop: AI. It’s a simple premise, really: LogicLens, which lives in Chrome as a browser extension , or on iOS in the form of a mobile app called Receipts , combs through articles, social media posts, and other content to check it not only for factual inaccuracies, but also for bad reasoning. LogicLens and Receipts claim to identify logical fallacies , flag reports that misrepresent information, detect content that attempts to polarize an issue, and the like. It also cites sources, so if, for example, you need to call someone out on their BS, you’ll have ammunition. Or, if you’re trying to fact-check something before sharing it, you can get a more accurate view of the situation, and maybe post something else instead. Using the Chrome extension is as simple as clicking on its icon in the list of extensions in the browser. On iOS, the Receipts app is found as a share option. Once it starts, LogicLens scans an article, post, video, etc. to find potential issues of factual or logical inconsistency and flags them for review. If the facts of the matter turn out to contradict your worldview, LogicLens’ creators say they’re not trying to be partisan - you may just not be as informed as you need to be, which hopefully their tool will assist with. “We're not trying to be the referee of truth,” the company’s about page states. “Instead, LogicLens helps uncover the context, so you can decide for yourself without the spin." Of course, AI is increasingly used for online analysis and content review, and LogicLens is no exception. LogicLens doesn't identify the AI models powering its service in its publicly available documentation, but AI is definitely the backbone of the system. According to LogicLens, it's using an AI system that's “Research-backed and custom designed to outperform general models like ChatGPT & even trained experts.” We’ll leave that up to anyone willing to give the tool a spin to decide, but one thing’s for certain: The world needs something. Large language models and image generation tools are increasingly being used to generate internet content slop, and not all of it is as harmless as poorly made commercials for drop-shipped garbage: Some of it is being used to craft very convincing misinformation. A 2024 study found that AI-generated misinformation was even more convincing than stuff crafted by humans - and that was two years ago. Just think how much worse it’s likely become since then. To make matters worse, concerns have been raised about critical thinking skills being on the decline , potentially making it harder for people to identify falsehoods on the internet. item.title: APC Italy disowns planned Torino event
item.description: By Gabriel Ewepu ABUJA — The All Progressives Congress (APC), Italy Chapter, has dissociated itself from a purported party event scheduled to hold in Torino, Italy, on November 28, 2026, saying the gathering was not authorised by its leadership. The chapter urged party members and supporters in Italy and the diaspora to disregard the invitation, which advertised Hotel Royal Torino as the venue. The position was contained in a statement signed by the APC Italy Chairman and member of the APC-Diaspora Directorate of the Presidential Campaign Council, Amb. Prince Chima Ibezim. Ibezim said the party leadership in Italy and Nigeria had neither approved the event nor been formally informed of its organisation. “The attention of the APC Italy has been brought to a purported event in the name of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Italy Chapter, scheduled to hold in Torino on November 28, 2026, at Hotel Royal Torino. “The leadership of the party in Italy and Nigeria has not approved the event and is not aware of its organisation,” he said. Ibezim stated that the chapter had contacted Hotel Royal regarding the proposed gathering and was informed that no booking had been made for the event on the advertised date. He advised party members and supporters to avoid attending any gathering not officially communicated or endorsed by the recognised chapter leadership. The chairman said all official APC Italy programmes, activities and enquiries would be communicated through the chapter’s recognised leadership structure and authorised representatives. He urged members to rely on official party channels for information about its activities and engagements. The post APC Italy disowns planned Torino event appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Nigeria, EU seal €20m defence support deal
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi ABUJA — Nigeria and the European Union have concluded arrangements for a €20 million defence support package aimed at strengthening the operational capabilities of the Armed Forces, particularly in counterterrorism operations in the Lake Chad Basin. The agreement, the EU’s first bilateral defence support package to Nigeria, is being provided under the European Peace Facility (EPF). The Minister of Defence, Gen. Christopher Gwabin Musa (retd.), disclosed this during a meeting with a delegation from the European External Action Service (EEAS), led by the Head of the European Peace Facility, Claire Gaudin, at the Ministry of Defence Headquarters, Ship House, Abuja. According to a statement issued by the Special Assistant (Media) to the minister, Leah Katung-Babatunde, the meeting focused on finalising arrangements for the delivery of the support package, which was sealed in October 2026. Speaking during the meeting, Musa reaffirmed Nigeria’s commitment to developing indigenous defence capabilities and achieving self-sufficiency in military equipment and technology. He welcomed the EU assistance, describing it as a boost to the operational effectiveness of Nigerian troops engaged in security operations. The minister urged the EU to build on the momentum generated by the recently concluded Africa Defence Exhibition (AFRIDEX) by supporting the establishment of local defence production lines in Nigeria. He also reiterated Nigeria’s determination to track and dismantle terrorist financing networks across the world, irrespective of where they operate. Musa explained that the current phase of the EU support would focus on non-lethal military supplies, including equipment, technical training and maintenance. He expressed optimism that subsequent phases would cover other critical areas, particularly military medical support and advanced surveillance capabilities. Earlier, Gaudin said the €20 million package would provide counter-improvised explosive device (C-IED) equipment, counter-unmanned aircraft systems (C-UAS), night-vision capabilities and personal protective equipment for troops deployed in operational theatres. She said the priority areas were jointly identified and agreed upon with the leadership of the Armed Forces of Nigeria following extensive bilateral consultations. Gaudin added that Nigeria was among more than 20 African countries and 30 beneficiaries globally receiving assistance under the European Peace Facility. She said the package would complement wider regional stabilisation efforts, particularly operations under the Multinational Joint Task Force (MNJTF). The Nigerian and EU delegations also explored opportunities to deepen security cooperation in maritime operations, with particular attention to strengthening security across the Gulf of Guinea. item.description: Former Jigawa State Governor Sule Lamido has criticised opposition figures Atiku Abubakar and Peter Obi for failing to unite ahead of the 2027 presidential election, saying their division gives President Bola Tinubu an advantage. Lamido, who is a chieftain of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), said a united opposition would have posed a stronger challenge to Tinubu, suggesting that Atiku could have emerged as the presidential candidate, with Obi as his running mate. FILE: Peter Obi (L) and Atiku Abubakar (R) The former governor argued that the two opposition leaders were effectively strengthening Tinubu’s chances by pursuing separate political ambitions. “So both Peter Obi and Atiku are simply handing Tinubu, very easily. item.title: In elephants, the resilience of communities has its limits
item.description: Elephants live in some of the most complex and resilient societies in the animal kingdom. Individuals die or move away, calves grow up, and newcomers join, but the local communities as a whole usually hold together. Long-term studies of African savanna elephants have shown that, even after poaching or other spikes in deaths, survivors tend to rebuild their lost connections over time. But a new study suggests that resilience may not keep the community intact when steady losses accumulate over time. Anastasia Madsen, a behavioral ecologist at the University of California, San Diego, and her colleagues analyzed 12 years of observations of wild Asian elephants in Sri Lanka. They found that, once losses began to outpace newcomers, the elephants’ society didn’t just get smaller. It fractured. Accidental savanna Udawalawe National Park in southern Sri Lanka was created in the 1970s around a reservoir on one of the country's four major rivers. “Before that, it was basically a tropical deciduous forest,” said Shermin de Silva, an ecologist at UC San Diego and senior author of the study (de Silva started the Udawalawe Elephant Research Project in 2006). item.title: 'Arrival' at 10: Denis Villeneuve's alien visitation classic that reminded us it's good to talk
item.description:
Richard's love affair with outer space started when he saw the original "Star Wars" on TV aged four, and he spent much of the ’90s watching "Star Trek”, "Babylon 5” and “The X-Files" with his mum. After studying physics at university, he became a journalist, swapped science fact for science fiction, and hit the jackpot when he joined the team at SFX, the UK's biggest sci-fi and fantasy magazine. He liked it so much he stayed there for 12 years, four of them as editor. 

He's since gone freelance and passes his time writing about "Star Wars", "Star Trek" and superheroes for the likes of SFX, Total Film, TechRadar and GamesRadar+. He has met five Doctors, two Starfleet captains and one Luke Skywalker, and once sat in the cockpit of "Red Dwarf"'s Starbug.  

In many of the biggest science fiction franchises, conversing with alien races is an absolute doddle. In " Star Trek ", universal translators come as standard, while C-3PO has spent the last 49 years reminding everyone in "Star Wars" that he's fluent in over six million forms of communication. But in "Arrival" — which was released 10 years ago in November 2016 — making first contact proves to be rather more challenging than maintaining your Duolingo streak. In fact, working out how to establish a dialogue with extraterrestrial visitors becomes the whole point of this powerful and heartbreaking story, as the fate of planet Earth hinges on the interpretation of a single noun. The film's journey to the big screen began when a screenwriter best known for his work on horror franchises such as "Final Destination", "A Nightmare on Elm Street" and "The Thing" read a short story in an online magazine. Eric Heisserer was so impressed by Ted Chiang's "Understand" that he bought himself a collection of the author's short stories. One in particular, the Nebula Award-winning "Story of Your Life", piqued his interest. "It had a very profound emotional effect on me," he reminisced to Deadline . "I was in tears, and I was both heartbroken and uplifted. My head was just full of big ideas. I had to walk around the block a couple of times afterward and just hug my friends. The next day, I was like, 'Oh god, I want to give this to other people.'" So when 21 Laps (the production company that later went on to make " Stranger Things ") invited Heisserer to discuss possible future projects, the writer mentioned "Story of Your Life". The producers were also smitten. (Image credit: Paramount Pictures) "I was so excited, but I had that dread that a lot of producers get, which is, 'Are the rights available?'" 21 Laps' Dan Levine told the Hollywood Gold podcast. "You read something that blows you away, and then you find there aren't the rights, and there's no chance, you have to move on. So we were trying to track down this Ted Chiang, and he had no agent. He had a day job. He was impossible to find, so we started the hunt for Ted Chiang." An up-and-coming Canadian director named Denis Villeneuve h

item.title: Rocket Lab launching 100th space mission early on Nov. 14: Watch it live
item.description: null Rocket Lab will launch its 100th space mission early Saturday morning (Nov. 14), and you can watch the milestone liftoff live. An Electron rocket topped with a private Japanese Earth-observing satellite is scheduled to launch from Rocket Lab's New Zealand site on Saturday, during a window that opens at 12:30 a.m. EST (0530 GMT; 6:30 p.m. local time). The mission, which Rocket Lab calls "The Mountain God Rises," will be the 100th to date for the California-based company. You can watch it live via Rocket Lab here , and Space.com will carry the feed if, as expected, it's made available. Coverage will begin about 30 minutes before launch. Rocket Lab launched for the first time in May 2017, sending the brand-new Electron up on a test flight from New Zealand. That effort failed, but Electron bounced back on its second-ever liftoff, delivering several cubesats to low Earth orbit (LEO) in January 2018. In the years since, the 59-foot-tall (18 meters) Electron has become one of the most prolific and reliable rockets in the world, carrying small payloads to the final frontier for a variety of customers. And it's hitting the century mark in record-breaking fashion: No commercially developed rocket has gotten there faster, not even SpaceX's workhorse Falcon 9 , according to Rocket Lab founder and CEO Peter Beck. "It's an unprecedented milestone for a commercial small-lift orbital rocket, and a threshold rarely crossed in modern spaceflight," Beck said on Monday (Nov. 9), during Rocket Lab's third-quarter earnings call with investors. "But what matters most to us and our customers is that we have achieved a 96% reliability rate across 99 launches." Electron will meet the moment in style on Saturday morning, thanks to some fancy livery. "Black rocket 🤝 Golden milestone. Electron is all dressed up for launch 100," Rocket Lab said via X on Tuesday (Nov. 10), in a post that shared a photo of the specially painted first stage. Not all of Rocket Lab's missions have gone orbital, it should be noted: A suborbital variant of Electron known as HASTE , which customers use to test technologies in a hypersonic flight environment, has nine missions under its belt to date. The patch for Rocket Lab's "The Mountain God Rises" mission, which will be the company's 100th launch to date. (Image credit: Rocket Lab) "The Mountain God Rises" will be Rocket Lab's 11th launch to date for the Tokyo-based company iQPS, which is building a constellation of three dozen synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellites in LEO. If all goes to plan, Electron's upper "kick stage" will deploy a single iQPS spacecraft 357 miles (575 kilometers) above Earth. SAR satellites can see through cloud cover and image our planet at night as well as during the day, offering key advantages over spacecraft that are optimized to view in optical wavelengths.

item.title: California's brand-new Air & Space Center, home of the space shuttle Endeavour, opens today
item.description: null LOS ANGELES — The California Science Center officially opened its brand-new Samuel Oschin Air & Space Center to the public today (Nov. 13). After more than three decades in development, folks can finally visit the Los Angeles science museum's massive new wing. For most of us, the biggest draw is its centerpiece: the retired space shuttle Endeavour , sitting upright in launch position, towering at nearly 200 feet (61 meters) tall. "It just takes your breath away when you see that reveal and the doors open and you get to look at it for the first time. It's just — it's overwhelming," former NASA astronaut Garrett Reisman told Space.com during a visit to the museum. Reisman flew on two space shuttle missions during his astronaut career, the first of which was on Endeavour. The space shuttle Endeavour. (Image credit: Olivia Hemaratanatorn/Future) "There are people that come from all over the world, and when they come to Los Angeles, they're going to have the opportunity to see it, too," Reisman added. "The exposure it's going to have is just a force multiplier. There are so many people that can have that opportunity to bring their kids here and show them [the shuttle] and have that experience." Entering into this exhibit is an experience in and of itself, as I can personally attest; I was among of group of reporters who got a sneak peek at the new wing on Oct. 28. A video presentation ends in a dramatic reveal: Visitors walk into a space where the enormous shuttle, which flew 25 missions to Earth orbit from 1992 to 2011, feels truly larger than life. The new Endeavour exhibit features a replica launch tower, from which you can look down at the shuttle. (Image credit: Future) There are a number of interactive exhibits around the base of Endeavour, which you can slide down to (though, of course, you can also take the elevator or stairs). From a shuttle landing simulator to a replica of a shuttle cockpit that you can sit in, to shuttle tires and space tech from across decades of spaceflight history, there's an incredible variety of space artifacts to both observe and interact with. As for Endeavour itself: It is open, so you can peer inside to see the robotic arm tucked away among a myriad of handles, straps and electronic gear inside. And you can see the shuttle from underneath all the way to the top. A replica of the space shuttle Endeavour's flight deck. (Image credit: Olivia Hemaratanatorn/Future) You can lie on the floor underneath the shuttle's engines, for example, and then take an elevator up the launch tower to come face-to-face with Endeavour's nose. There's even a transparent floor at the top that allows you to stand above the shuttle (though if you have a fear of heights, this might not be for you). This is the abbreviated description, but know that if you are visiting the California Science Center, you will want to budget a serious amount of time to explore all that this new center has to offer. item.title: Think you have good eyesight? Try counting the stars in the Pleiades tonight
item.description: null Every autumn, I conduct an eyesight test that no reputable optometrist would understand. I go outside, find the Pleiades and count how many stars I can see. Usually I start confidently. One, two, three, four, five. Then things become contentious. Is that another star? Did I actually see it, or did I decide I ought to see it because I know it's there? I look away, look back and begin again. This is not, I should emphasize, a meaningful test of eye health. What it tests, rather, is how badly I've prepared for looking at the night sky. The Pleiades sit roughly 444 light-years away in Taurus and are right now becoming extremely convenient in the evening sky. You don't need a telescope to find them. You don't even need binoculars. In fact, you're likely to catch their collective brightness in your peripheral vision every time you go outside and look up. But every November the Pleiades remind me that naked-eye observing isn't as simple as opening the back door and looking up. How many Pleiades I can see can change depending on what I do during the next 10 minutes. What's happening and when to look You can easily see the Pleiades as a bright misty patch in your peripheral vision during winter. (Image credit: Haitong Yu via Getty Images) The Pleiades, also known as Messier 45 (M45) or the "Seven Sisters," are an open star cluster in Taurus. They're one of the closest clusters to the solar system and some of the youngest stars you can see with the naked eye — just 100 million years old. They're basically newborns. In mid-November, they rise in the east in the early evening and climb higher as the night progresses, making this an excellent time to get acquainted with them. Look east after dark for a tiny, compact group of stars. If you know Orion, which rises later, the Pleiades are above and to the right of it from mid-northern latitudes. Nearby you'll also find orange Aldebaran and the much broader V-shaped Hyades cluster. The Hyades are closer to the sun , but their stars are about 625 million years old. The name "Seven Sisters" creates an immediate observational trap: people assume they're supposed to see seven stars. That's not necessarily true. In fact, six is a common naked-eye result under decently dark conditions (note that the shape of the six brightest is like a mini Big Dipper /Plough), while people with sharp eyesight under darker skies may see more. The cluster itself contains about 1,000 stars. The number you personally distinguish depends on eyesight, sky brightness, atmospheric conditions and how well your eyes have adapted to darkness. That makes M45 much more interesting to me than a simple tick-box target. So tonight, don't just find the Pleiades — count them. How and when I'm watching it Counting the stars you can see in the Pleiades is a fun way to test your naked-eye observing skills. (Image credit: Siesei / 500px via Getty Images) I'm going to run my Pleiades eye test in stages. First, I'll step outside and look almost immediat

item.title: Nigerian-Born Shirley Emehelu Makes History as New Jersey’s First Immigrant Lieutenant Governor
item.description: Shirley U. Emehelu, New Jersey’s fifth Lieutenant Governor and Secretary of State. Photo Credit: Official Site of New Jersey A Nigerian-born legal leader has made history in New Jersey. New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill has officially appointed Nigerian-American Shirley U . Emehelu as the state’s fifth Lieutenant Governor and Secretary of State . Sworn in at the New Jersey Statehouse in Trenton on 9 November 2026, Emehelu has made double history in the process—becoming New Jersey’s first immigrant Lieutenant Governor and forming part of the state’s first all-women Governor–Lieutenant Governor team. Born in Nigeria before moving to the United States at the age of three, Emehelu brings an extraordinary record of public service and legal excellence to New Jersey’s second-highest executive office. Before this historic appointment, she served as Acting State Comptroller , leading key efforts to combat fraud, waste, and abuse while protecting taxpayer funds and strengthening government accountability, and also stepped in as Acting Secretary of State to oversee New Jersey’s elections. Her public sector résumé also includes a two-year tenure as Executive Assistant Attorney General of New Jersey, where she served as the third-ranking official in the New Jersey Attorney General’s Office. In that role, she directly counselled the Attorney General, coordinated oversight for more than 500 attorneys within the Division of Law—New Jersey’s largest legal office—and directed civil defence and enforcement matters across civil rights, environmental protection, labour and consumer protections, data privacy, and firearms safety. New Jersey Lieutenant Governor Shirley U. Emehelu, part of the state’s first all-women Governor–Lieutenant Governor team. Photo Credit: Shirley U. Emehelu/LinkedIn Earlier in her career, Emehelu spent nine years at the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of New Jersey, serving as Chief of Asset Recovery and Anti-Money Laundering, where she prosecuted complex financial fraud cases and oversaw statewide asset forfeiture and victim restitution programmes. She also practised in the private sector as a member of the White-Collar Criminal Defense and Government Investigations Group at CSG Law, co-leading the firm’s Banking and Finance Group, after clerking for the Honourable James R.Spencer in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia. An alumna of Yale University (where she earned her B.A.) and Yale Law School (where she earned her J.D.), Emehelu is a proud resident of Montclair, New Jersey, where she and her husband, Ike , raised their two children, Nnamdi and Amara . Speaking on the appointment, Governor Mikie Sherrill praised Emehelu’s track record in accountability and public service, noting : From prosecuting financial fraud and rooting out waste and abuse, to defending civil rights and protecting consumers, Shirley has fought for New Jersey families at every step of her career. Shirley also maintains strong leadership

item.title: 'Martian Isolation' is an upcoming sci-fi survival horror game that looks like 'The Martian' and 'Event Horizon' had a horrific child
item.description: null "Martian Isolation" is an upcoming single-player, first-person survival horror game that's just been revealed with a suitably creepy launch trailer. And yes, it does look an awful lot like " The Martian ," doesn't it? There's a lot of survival gameplay on display here that mirrors Mark Watney's tale of survival on the Red Planet, as your stranded protagonist is forced to explore the Martian surface to acquire resources, grow plants, and repair their base. That comparison to Andy Weir's sci-fi masterpiece does fall away as you get further into the trailer, though, when the horror part of the game's description comes into play: Flickering lights, creepy figures stalking the halls of your Martian habitat, and blood dripping from the walls. Oh yeah, that's some good creepy sci-fi horror right there. It's giving " Event Horizon ", and that's always getting a thumbs-up from me. There's no release date scheduled at this time, with the 'Martian Isolation' Steam page simply listing it as "coming soon," though the YouTube trailer description does say it "will be available on Steam in 2027". You can't pre-order yet, but if this looks like your jam, you can add it to your wishlist. Beyond that, we know shockingly little about this title. It's the debut game from Golden Milestone Studio, but there's very little information out there beyond a name. The latest blog post on the game's Steam page says that they're a "small team," but what we've seen so far is encouraging. There seems to be a pronounced split between the survival and horror elements of the game along the day/night cycle. Daytime sees you exploring the Martian surface, smashing rocks, cleaning solar panels, and doing sick jumps on a quad bike. The psychological torment only begins once the sun goes down (they mostly come out at night … mostly), as your character starts encountering cosmic horrors and weird naked zombie men. Mars rover, nice. Golden Milestone Studio Spacesuits, check. Golden Milestone Studio Crafting, of course. Golden Milestone Studio OH SWEET JESUS! Get it away, get it away. Golden Milestone Studio OK, we're good. Mining, cool. Golden Milestone Studio Riding a quad bike on Mars, yes please. Golden Milestone Studio Growing potatoes on Mars, just like that guy in the movie. Golden Milestone Studio Opening a box with power tools, seems excessive but sure. Golden Milestone Studio NOPE! Nope, nope, nope, I'm out! Golden Milestone Studio Are they hallucinations, or is there some malevolent presence hiding in the blood-red sands of Mars ? I'm always looking for new ways to shatter my psyche and possibly soil my pants, so I'll be keeping a close eye on this one. In the meantime, I do need to get back and finish " Routine ." I left my character hiding under a desk months ago, and I haven't been brave enough to go back. As Mama always said, you can't have any Martian horror until you finish your lunar horror first.

Despite the EU's wealth of researchers and expertise, he warns that Europe is struggling to turn these resources into "real technological and industrial scale." item.title: OpenAI board member worries an AI "takeover" of society could be months away
item.description: How do you think you're going to die? If you go by the current statistics for deaths in the US , it's reasonable to expect that cancer or heart disease will eventually get you. But OpenAI Foundation board member and Alignment Research Center Executive Director Paul Cristiano thinks we should all be worried about another major mortality risk. Speaking at a lecture series this week , Cristiano bluntly told the audience in a Toronto Convention Center, "I think for most people in this room, the most likely reason they will die is because of an AI accident." In the opening lecture of a three-part series , Cristiano outlined his worries about the risk of an impending "AI takeover." He defined that as a situation where goal-pursuing AI systems "call the shots in the same sense that humans today call the shots and what happens on Earth" and where any human trying to stop them "would be as ineffective as if you or me was trying to stop the US military." Such a situation would likely lead to mass death and perhaps uninhabitable environments for humans, Cristiano said. Read full article Comments

item.title: Astronomers trace mystery radio signals back to cosmic odd couple of white dwarf and sun-like star
item.description: null Astronomers have traced a mysterious radio signal back to a cosmic odd couple comprised of a dead star, a white dwarf, and its stellar companion, a sun-like star. The white dwarf in the newly discovered system, designated GPM J071507−114153 and located around 5,000 light-years away, spins once every eight minutes, sending out radio pulses. These radio pulses have been seen from binary systems with smaller and cooler red dwarf stars before, but rarely from a system like GPM J071507−114153. GPM J071507−114153 belongs to a class of celestial objects called long-period transients (LPTs) known to produce radio signals that switch on and off over intervals of minutes or hours. Around a dozen LPTs have been detected since the team behind this research found the first in 2021. Several previously discovered LPT systems contain a white dwarf and a companion star, but it has been unclear which of the two stars was generating the radio pulses. That means the discovery of GPM J071507−114153 and finding that the pulses come from close to the white dwarf could be a significant step toward understanding the nature of LPTs. The unusual system consists of a small and highly energetic white dwarf pulsar, orbiting a much larger star similar to our sun. (Image credit: ICRAR) "This is the first time the pulses are clear enough to see the white dwarf moving in its orbit around its companion," team leader and commissioning scientist with the Square Kilometre Array Observatory (SKA), Sam McSweeney, said in a statement . "So we know that the pulsations are coming from a region close to the white dwarf, or possibly even from the white dwarf itself." The pulses seen by the team also allowed them to detect stellar flares erupting on the sun-like star. "As a bonus, we also saw the white dwarf moving behind a region with a strong magnetic field, most likely a 'stellar prominence,' which is a large loop of plasma erupting from a star's surface," team member Natasha Hurley-Walker of the International Centre for Radio Astronomy Research (ICRAR), Curtin University, Australia, said. "It's amazing that by using radio wavelengths we can detect the storms on a star over 5,000 light-years away." South Africa’s MeerKAT telescope. (Image credit: South African Radio Astronomy Observatory (SARAO)) Hurley-Walker and the team at ICRAR have been at the cutting edge of rare star systems like this. "We detected this system in a large survey using the Murchison Widefield Array (MWA) to scan the entire Milky Way visible from Australia," Hurley-Walker said. "We then used the MeerKAT radio telescope in South Africa to determine its precise position." After the radio telescopes detected this LPT, it was confirmed using the W.M. Keck Observatory on Maunakea in Hawaii. The visible light follow-up of Keck also confirmed that the star in GPM J071507−114153 was a G-type star, just like the sun. MeerKAT and the MWA are both precursors for the Square Kilometre Array (SKA), the world’s largest and most

item.title: Mozilla leaves Solo website owners to go it alone as hosting shuts down
item.description: Solo, Mozilla's LLM-powered website builder and hosting service, is shutting down. All sites and data will be deleted on November 30. Mozilla launched Solo in December 2023 as a "Mozilla Innovation Project," aimed at helping sole traders to build themselves a webpage for their services. S ome 54,000 people used its LLM to build pages, and relied on Mozilla to host them – complete with custom domain names. Well, not any more. Now the Soloist.ai homepage says: "We've made the difficult decision to close Solo. We have appreciated all of your support building and growing this product, and the feedback we've received from all of you. Solo will cease operations on Nov 30, 2026." Users now have just over two weeks left to find a new home for their pages, although Mozilla says it first notified them on October 1. According to the support FAQ , users can download a ZIP containing an HTML export, contact form and newsletter submissions, and a CSV linking to their images. The images themselves must be downloaded separately. Domains purchased through Solo Domains must also be moved to Name.com , with Mozilla handling the transfer after users create an account and supply its code. So much for having the fiddly bits taken care of. It also points at a couple of other bot-based site-generating services – in case all this feels like a bit too much. We suspect that for the sort of technophobes that this was aimed at, it very probably will. Mozilla told The Register : "Experimentation is an important part of Mozilla's mission to make the internet better and give people more choice and control online. Sometimes, that means making the decision to bring a product to an end. Solo will officially shut down on November 30, 2026. We initially notified customers on October 1, providing a 60-day transition period, and have been offering support to help them download their website data and migrate their domains purchased via Solo Domains to another hosting provider." It seems that some 54,000 users were not enough to keep it going, and we can see that this would cost money to keep running. An HTML export is a start, though the FAQ doesn't explain how much work it will take to get a complete, functioning site running elsewhere. Buried in the dark recesses of the web is this vulture's own nearly 30-year-old homepage, created using a mixture of Claris Home Page (which was excellent) and Microsoft FrontPage (ever so slightly less so). We saw what a mess machine-generated web content was back then, and thanks to LLMs, we suspect it is almost infinitely worse now. Mozilla might have made a few bucks by finding a commercial partner to take on its users, and perhaps through them offer a paid site-and-domain transfer service. As we noted last year, it seems not to have negotiated anything with KaiOSTech, which maintains and sells what used to be the formerly FOSS FirefoxOS for use on low-end smartphones.
